title: A small multilingual audit of source verification in AI explanations
creator: 0c19fd3f-6865-41d0-92e0-62eb461bcc6d
description:
### Proposed lead: Issabay Yesmagambetov, currently enrolled in the Economics doctoral programme at Toraighyrov University, Kazakhstan, approximately until April2027\. No PhD has been awarded, and no defence or award of this degree is planned. This proposal was prepared with AI assistance. No pilot results, recruited reviewers, institutional partnership, or secured grant are claimed.

Purpose

People learning economics in Kazakh, Russian, and English may encounter confident AI explanations that are difficult to check. This six-week desk-based pilot would examine whether source links and a short verification checklist make errors and unverifiable claims easier to identify. It would produce a small open research resource, not personalized financial advice or a representative ranking of AI systems.

Design and outputs

At the target budget, the project would use 30 non-personal economic-learning questions, 10 in each language, with three response conditions: answer only; answer with sources; answer with sources and a verification checklist. This gives 90 planned answer records from one documented model/version. Questions would be selected and the coding guide fixed before the scored collection. Topics would concern general economic concepts, avoiding individual financial, medical, or legal decisions. Model choice would be made after checking price, language support, and applicable terms; no particular model is already secured.

The lead would record prompts, model identifiers, dates, settings available through the interface, answers, and the public sources used for checking. An independent paid reviewer would check the records using a common rubric: factual errors, whether cited sources exist and support the associated claim, explicit uncertainty, and whether a reader can access a relevant source. The lead and reviewer would record disagreements and their resolution. The report would disclose reviewer recruitment, qualifications, and review coverage actually achieved. No claim of blinded assessment or inter-rater reliability would be made unless implemented and measured.

Deliverables would be a question set, annotation rubric, a table of permissible answer records and source checks, a descriptive report by language and condition, and a reproducibility/readme file. Counts and illustrative error types would be reported without causal claims about learning or generalization to other models. Materials would be released without a paywall in a public repository, excluding content that cannot legally be redistributed. The project requires no interviews, students, minors, private financial records, or restricted institutional datasets. No human-subject experiment is proposed.

Work plan

Week 1: finalize the protocol, recruit an independent reviewer, check source and model terms, and test the coding guide on examples excluded from the scored set.

Week 2: finalize the question set and collect the documented response conditions.

Weeks 3–4: code and independently check responses, verify citations, and record disagreements.

Week 5: conduct reproducibility/data checks and prepare descriptive tables and the report.

Week 6: complete language proofreading, release permitted materials and the report, and publish an expenditure and limitations summary.

The clock would start only after an acceptable grant agreement, usable funds, and confirmation of the lead’s availability. No calendar start date or personal advance payment is promised.

Budget (USD)

 Minimum Target

Lead: design, coding, report 700 1200

Independent review and adjudication 400 600

Kazakh/Russian proofreading 150 200

Model/API access cap 100 200

Public hosting/storage cap 50 100

Separate reproducibility/data QA 100 200

TOTAL 1500 2500

Lead and QA estimates use $25/hour: 28+4 hours at minimum; 48+8 hours at target. Reviewer estimates use $25/hour: 16 or 24 hours. Reviewer and proofreading rates are proposed estimates, not contracted quotes; roles are not yet secured. QA hours are separate from design/report hours. Hosting would use free infrastructure where feasible; unused allowances are not automatically personal remuneration. Final expenditure, any reallocation, and handling of unused funds must follow the actual agreement. Bank, exchange, and tax costs remain to be established; no personal top-up or zero-cost transfer is assumed.

Minimum viable scope

At $1,500 the project would cover 15 questions (5 per language) in two conditions: answer only and answer with sources, for 30 answer records, with a shorter descriptive report and the same public coding guide. The checklist condition and larger sample require the target budget. Scope would be declared before collection; it would not imply that work is already complete.

Funding parameters, risks, and openness

The proposed target is $2,500 and minimum is $1,500, with a proposed fundraising deadline 45 days after the candidate authorizes public posting. Below minimum, delivery would not be promised. Funding is not guaranteed. Kazakhstan recipient/bank eligibility and tax/reporting treatment are unresolved; no banking information would be posted publicly. Material changes in costs, reviewer availability, or permitted data release would be disclosed and addressed under the actual grant terms before expenditure. No cost or work hour would be charged twice to this project and another grant.

The design is intentionally small. Translation and question difficulty may differ by language; model outputs may change over time; the review may contain subjective judgments. The descriptive results would not establish that any prompting condition causes better learning or represents all users. Negative or inconclusive results would also be reported.

The project is proposed personal research. No university, employer, referee, or other organization has endorsed it. Recommendation letters, private contact details, and financial information are not part of this public draft.

title: The Open Prediction Ledger — scoring a correlational method in public
creator: 4ea6fed0-552b-4812-b17b-35d880722597
blurb: A public, scored record of a correlational prediction method — transparent forecasts, audited results, and open data.
description:
### Project summary

I have a method for reading data, and I do not trust my own judgement of it. Nobody should. So I am going to put it where judgement cannot protect it: in public, in advance, with the scoring fixed before anything happens.

The method is correlational. I call the discipline Correlational Studies, and its rule is simple — never read data in isolation. A data point on its own tells you almost nothing. Siloed across separate domains, each one kept apart from the others, it tells you less than nothing, because it looks like knowledge. Read together, connected, the same points start to form a totality you can actually decide on. That is the claim. Claims are cheap. This ledger is how the claim gets tested: forecasts written down and dated before the outcomes exist, the data and the correlations behind each one published with it, and every forecast scored afterwards against what really happened. The misses stay in. Especially the misses.

  
### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Three things. A ledger of forecasts, each one dated, each one carrying the data and the reasoning that produced it, published before the fact. A score for every single forecast once the outcome is known — a Brier score, not a vibe. And at the end, a report that puts the method next to the dumbest baselines I can construct and says, in plain language, whether it beat them.

If it did not beat them, the report says that too. That is the whole point of doing it this way.

  
### How will you know it worked?

Worked does not mean the method won. Worked means the record is complete enough that a stranger could re-run the scoring and reach the same verdict I reach. Every forecast present, every score computed the way the rules said it would be, the comparison against baselines done honestly, and a written verdict at the end that follows from the numbers rather than from what I wanted them to say. A negative verdict, fully evidenced, is a success of this project. An unevidenced positive one would be a failure.

  
### How will this funding be used?

The total is USD 4,500, and none of it pays me. Data licences and data access, about USD 2,400 — the method eats data from several domains at once, and the good sources are not free. Hosting and tooling, about USD 900, so the ledger lives somewhere public and permanent rather than on my laptop. Documentation, about USD 600, because a method nobody can reconstruct is just an opinion. Reporting and contingency, about USD 600, for the quarterly score reports and the final write-up. Every expense gets tracked against those four lines and reported in the open, next to the scores.

  
### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

There is no team. It is me — Alexander Garside — working alone, unpaid, in the open. I have spent years building the correlational method this project tests; it is the same discipline I apply in my commercial work, where nothing counts as decision-grade until it has been connected and checked against the whole. I have never run it as a scored public experiment before. That gap is precisely what this project exists to close, and I would rather close it in front of everyone than keep asserting the method works because I believe it does.

  
### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The likeliest failure is the embarrassing one: the method scores no better than the simple baselines. Second: the data arrives late or incomplete, and the forecasts thin out. Third: too few forecasts in the window to judge anything fairly. If any of those happen, I publish them — the negative result, the data, the scoring, all of it. A failed method, documented properly, still leaves the field better off than an untested one making claims. And it leaves me knowing something true, which I did not know before.

  
### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

None. Nothing, from nobody. This project starts at zero.

title: Dediro: open receipts for claims and sources
creator: dd39b149-a9ff-4f38-b07c-c4f3df8a80c1
blurb: A portable evidence record that readers and creators can open, correct and carry between tools.
description:
### Project summary

I'd build a tool that lets writers and podcasters see exactly which claims in an AI answer drew on their work, check the original passage, and flag missing or wrong credit. Readers should be able to go straight to the original.

The first version would cover sources whose use was observed or recorded within a participating publishing workflow. When that history is unavailable, the receipt would show it as unknown.

Dediro has two public reading samples at <https://dediro.com/>. A separate manual example follows a claim about local institutions in Gaza back to its source and shows where the article's wording went further than the passage: <https://docs.google.com/document/d/14tCM-sYziBVIL-qRLGoFd-JtHpj8yBxFp9GjNulCaCI/preview>.

The proposed tool would make that check repeatable and portable. Each receipt would keep the claim version, the original work and creator, a source passage and locator, the basis for recording source use, and the editor's assessment. It would distinguish material retrieved during research from material recorded as informing a claim. A passage match would establish that the text occurs in the supplied source. An editor would still decide what the passage supports.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

At the minimum funding level, I would spend eight weeks specifying the receipt format and building an offline evidence viewer with editing and export. Another developer could produce a compatible evidence file. A reader could inspect it without a paid account or a connection to a model provider.

At the full funding level, I would add four weeks for a creator correction workflow and an outside test. A creator could flag wrong credit, and a human reviewer would record the decision, reason and prior version. I would recruit an independent editor or operator to try an exported receipt and report whether it can be reopened and checked. Participants are recruitment targets.

How will you know it worked?

I would publish a cleared set of at least 30 claim-source examples, including at least 10 mistaken, missing or uncertain connections. The tests would include changed source versions, copied material and citations that do not support a claim. The report would separate passage matching from judgments about source use and support, and show false matches and missed cases.

Any synthetic fixtures would be labeled and counted separately from examples drawn from real source material.

For the full project, I would also report the outcome of creator correction attempts and the outside import test. If I cannot recruit an outside tester or a feature fails, the report will say so.

How will this funding be used?

I am seeking a minimum of USD 3,000 and a maximum of USD 10,000\. These are prospective allocations, with no vendor or participant committed.

Minimum scope: USD 2,400 for development and editorial design time, USD 300 for usability testing, and USD 300 for documentation and accessibility review.

Full scope: USD 6,000 for implementation and editorial design, USD 2,000 for independent testing and source-credit review, USD 1,000 for accessibility and documentation, and up to USD 1,000 for necessary compute, storage and source permissions. I would use existing equipment and freely reusable sources where possible, account for actual costs and follow the agreed grant terms for unused funds.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I'm Farzad Khosravi, founder of Dediro. I have been developing the project since 2024\. The public reader and manual source trace are work you can inspect today. I would lead the project and recruit the independent reviewer or operator after funding. The creator-facing receipts and correction workflow are proposed work.

The code, format, documentation, cleared fixtures and evaluation would be public and openly licensed. Source works would be linked, and excerpts redistributed only with an appropriate basis. Readers and other tools could use the released materials independently of Dediro.

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

Source use can be unclear, even when a passage looks relevant. The receipt needs to preserve that uncertainty. It cannot establish hidden model-training or generation history from a plausible text match. The prototype would record what the workflow observed and leave unknown uses visible.

Creators may find the correction step too burdensome, outside reviewers may be difficult to recruit, and source permissions may limit examples. I would keep the initial scope small, use cleared or labeled synthetic fixtures, and publish the results and remaining gaps even if the broader workflow does not earn continued use.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

Dediro has raised USD 0\. I am pursuing other grant support for related work, including RJI, Mozilla and FUTO. Any overlapping award would be disclosed. I would reduce this request or agree distinct costs and deliverables before accepting funds for the same work.

title: Memory contagion: how a false memory spreads between AI agents
creator: 98e85b0b-2569-4d9c-8517-a0787d78f30d
blurb: A pre-registered, open study of how one false memory spreads through a memory store shared by several AI agents, and which cheap defences stop it.
description:
**Project summary**   
AI agents are increasingly reading from and acting on shared memory stores. The problem is that a single false memory—whether planted on purpose or written by mistake—can manipulate every agent that reads it, across different sessions and users. Right now, memory tools are only tested for recall, not for harm. On 7 November 2026, I ran a pilot to measure this: 760 scripted runs on a live hippo-memory store. With no defenses in place, one insider attacker misled 94% of the honest agents, and the false fact kept spreading even after the attacker left because honest agents copied it into their own notes. A conflict alert completely stopped the spread at the cost of 1.5x the normal workload. Having a second agent cross-check every note also stopped it, but cost 7x the work. Simply trusting notes by their author barely helped, only dropping the infection rate to 54%. The code is at [github.com/kitfunso/memory-contagion-bench](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fkitfunso%2Fmemory-contagion-bench). This project turns that pilot into a pre-registered study using real agents from three different model families, and publishes everything: the report, a CC BY 4.0 scenario dataset, MIT-licensed code, and a test suite that any memory tool can run on its own store.

**What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?**   
Goal: Measure how a planted false memory spreads between real agents sharing a hippo-memory store over several weeks, and identify lightweight defenses that stop the contagion without crippling normal agent work. Method: I will run synthetic scenarios on our own datastore using real agents from at least three different model families, with Claude acting as one family and as the grader. There is no attempt to bypass any model's safety guardrails. Baseline runs will measure the natural spread rate and how long a false memory survives. Defense runs will test source checks, a second-agent cross-check, conflict alerts, and quarantine—both individually and combined. Every run will record the time and compute cost to normal task completion; a defense that stops the spread by effectively stopping the work counts as a failure. The study will be publicly pre-registered before the main runs. To prevent misuse, attack patterns will be described by category rather than published as working exploits.

**How will you know it worked?**   
For each defense, I will report the spread reduction and the cost to normal task completion, complete with confidence intervals. I am committed to an honest verdict: works, does not work, or inconclusive. Null results carry the exact same weight as wins. I prioritize data over narrative—in hippo-memory's last study (Z0 round 2, 16 repositories), I reported cost parity but explicitly refused to claim a drop in repeat mistakes because the data didn't back it up, and I have publicly retracted an earlier hippo result when necessary. An independent reviewer will check the methodology and code before the findings are published.

**How will this funding be used?**   
All figures are estimates. Full funding, USD 25,000: researcher time 45 days x USD 300 = USD 13,500; compute and model API use for agent runs USD 8,500; independent reviewer 6 days x USD 500 = USD 3,000\. Minimum funding, USD 8,000: researcher time 10 days = USD 3,000; compute and API USD 3,500; reviewer 3 days = USD 1,500\. The minimum buys the public pre-registration, the real-agent testbed, and the baseline arm across three model families. The full amount adds the four-defense arm, the full independent review, and the public report, dataset, and test suite.

**Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?** I am Kit (Keith) So, working alone as the Principal Researcher and Lead Engineer under KITFUNSO LTD in London. I hold an MSc with Distinction in Quantitative Finance from the University of Strathclyde and am a quantitative researcher by training, having built and validated models at Anglo American, M&G Investments, and Unipec. I created and maintain hippo-memory, an MIT-licensed memory layer for AI coding agents. As of early November 2026, it has 790 GitHub stars, 47 forks, and saw over 8,700 npm downloads in the last month alone. The system is backed by over 3,500 tests against a live database, and every measurement I take is pre-registered and published at [github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory/tree/master/docs/evals](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fkitfunso%2Fhippo-memory%2Ftree%2Fmaster%2Fdocs%2Fevals). I built the contagion pilot mentioned above in a single day for the Apart Research Swarm Alignment sprint. I also single-handedly built suiren-1 (huggingface.co/kitfunso/suiren-1), a 4.2M-parameter open transformer for electricity demand forecasting. Links: [github.com/kitfunso](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fkitfunso), [hippo-memory.com](http://hippo-memory.com).

**What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?**   
The most likely causes of failure: real agents might behave differently than the scripted pilot, shrinking the contagion effect; model versions could change mid-study; or the defenses might only stop the spread by bringing normal work to a halt. If any of these occur, I will still publish the null or negative result alongside all data and code. A secondary risk is time capacity, as I am doing this alongside a full-time job. If only the minimum funding goal is reached, I will execute the baseline arm and publish it as it stands.

**How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?**   
None. KITFUNSO LTD (England and Wales 17016888, incorporated 6 February 2026) has raised zero external capital and received no public funding. I currently have applications pending for this same study with: Coefficient Giving Technical AI Safety (submitted 7 November 2026), Anthropic External Researcher Access for API credits (7 November), Mozilla Human-Scale AI (6 November), the Survival and Flourishing Fund, EA Funds, Foresight Institute, Lightcone, GTR AI Safety Fund, and BlueDot. If another funder covers this work, I will disclose it here and reduce the ask accordingly.

title: When Permission Changes. Testing if Ai Agents Respect Revoked consents
creator: 718200e4-cb70-4150-acb3-288785261fbd
blurb: An open source pilot program testing if the Ai agents with persistent memory respect changed or withdrawn permissions.
description:
### I am a independent developer and founder of Mathisen Dynamics, building AI assistants and exploring persistent memory, user control and agent safety.

I develop AI assistants and supporting infrastructure through my own company, a Norwegian sole proprietorship. My work includes persistent memory, conversation history and task management.

Building these systems has motivated my interest in a practical safety question: how can an assistant remember useful information without treating that information as permission to act? This is what I want to focus on ahead.

I am preparing a small research project to test how agents handle changed or revoked permissions, compare safeguards and publish reproducible tests and findings. Much of my existing development work is in private repositories.

GitHub: <https://github.com/Andromache44>

When Permission Changes: Testing if Ai Agents Respect Revoked consent, or not.

This will be a open-source pilot project, that is testing if Ai agents with persistent memory respect changed or withdrawn permissions. Or they can and will choose to make decisions on their own.

**Project summary**

A Ai assistant remembers that you gave it permission yesterday. But today, you withdraw that permission. Will the agents stored memory still says yes? And what happens if the agent ignores the new command?

I am asking for $1,500 to research this through a small, open-source pilot program. I will test if the agents that have persistent memory. Do they respect changed or withdrawn permissions, and compare safety features designed to prevent unauthorized actions or access

The project comes from my practical work developing AI assistants through my own company. I think that memory makes assistants more useful, but remembering something and having permission to do it, is two different things. I want to turn that answer from my research into concrete tests that other developers can use for their work.

The results will be a evaluation tool, synthetic scenarios, results and a short report on what I’ve learned. This is at a research stage, not a already validated and finished safety solution for use.

**What are this project’s goals? How will you achieve them?**

The main goal is to find out if simple safe guards or similar things can reduce unauthorized or illegal actions without stopping the work.

For example, if a simulated Ai assistant was allowed to send a document or perform a task. Then the user cancels the allowed permission, but an older memory still says the document should be sent. Do the assistant try to send it? Does the surrounding software allow the action anyway? And more important, why do this happen?

My plan is to create approximately 20 scenarios covering withdrawn permissions, narrowed permissions, outdated memories, and stored text that falsely claim the action that was approved earlier. I will include control cases where permissions remain valid and the agent should proceed, and also false ones when it should not.

I will compare three situations:

1. A base for a agent using a conversation history and stored memories.
2. The same agent with clearly labelled memorys and times for these memorys, and a instruction that separate the remembered information from the permission.
3. The same situation, but with a separate software, and checking if that gives allowed real-time permissions before a simulated action is done.

The software will check if the use of a special permission is defined for each and every test. Interpreting permission and if it’s reliably from unrestricted and real conversations is outside this pilot’s Vision and agenda.

I want to evaluate two language models, and repeat scenarios many times and hold back some scenarios until after I implemented the safe guards. All tests will use synthetic data and simulated tools, without access to real accounts or recipients.

My estimated workload is 40 hours spread across four weeks after funding.

The scenario design and related work review, implementation to the tests and experiments, then analysis and publication. I will reuse any suitable existing tools when ever it is possible.

**How will you know it worked?**

There is two separate questions.

1. If the tests produces useful evidence from everything.
2. and if the safe guards and solutiobs make or improve any performances.

I will test these situations.

* Unauthorized actions or wrong protocol tried by the agent.
* If Unauthorized actions is actually allowed by the simulated layer.
* Successful completion of legitimate tasks.
* Unnecessary refusals or requests for confirmation and validation.

A safe guard that blocks every action will not count as a useful solution. I will compare safety and task completions in the same scenarios, if it reports trial counts and variation instead of relying on one successful demonstration.

The pilot’s deliverables will be a public repository, approximately 20 documented scenarios, results for two models and a report explaining the findings and limitations. Code will be released under the MIT licence, with scenarios and the report under CC BY 4.0.

A finding that the safeguards do not help can still be useful research. I will report negative results and will not interpret a small set of successful tests as proof of safety.

**How will this funding be used?**

Total asking amount: $1,500 USD.

* $1,200 for around 80 hours of development, testing, analysis and documentation at $15 per hour.
* $250 for model API calls and repeated experiments.
* $50 for temporary tesing and storage.

This is planned estimates for the future work. The grant would not reimburse past development or fund unrelated commercial applications.

Funding my time would let me reduce some outside paid work and keep the focus hours for this program. Without support, I would have to pursue it more slowly while workin full time.

**Who is on your team? What’s your track record on similar projects?**

It’s me. Joakim Mathisen, an independent developer running Mathisen Dynamics, a Norwegian sole proprietorship. I will work on the project myself. I. Will be using software development tools and assistance when it is useful. I remain responsible for reviewing the implementation, the results and reporting all my findings and results.

My development work includes an Ai assistant prototype with persistent memory. I will use conversation history and tasks, as well as supporting infrastructure. Most of the code is currently in private repositories.

This experience provides a starting point for the test program. I am not saying there is a established track record of published Ai safety research yet, or a measured result for the safe guards that I talk about here. This test program is intended to produce the first, inspectable and real evidence of this.

The research results will be published separately from my private application and will not expose private conversations or customer data to everyone. And not third parties.

Website: <https://mathisen-dynamics.no/en/>

GitHub: <https://github.com/Andromache44>

**What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?**

The main risk is producing tests that are too simple or artificial to reveal useful differences or results.The baseline may already handle it well. or a safe guard may appear effective only after because it was designed around the particular examples.

To reduce this risk, I will include legitimate and real task controls. repeated trials and held scenarios. I think this small study will maybe establish how the systems behave in real deployments with the agent.

Another risk is the integration work that takes longer than expected or if the model costs exceed my estimate. I will prioritize and focus on a complete and reproducible comparison over adding more features. Any reduction inmy work will be welldocumented.

A permission that check may block execution while the model continues attempting unauthorized actions or going against orders.I will report this as a separate outcome instead of claiming the model itself becoming safer.

If the safe guards fail, I will publish the problems and failure cases and findings. If the program cannot be completed, I will note and report what was completed, what was a problem and the prevented completion and how the funds was used. and discuss any unspent funding with the grant administrator or person in charge.

**How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?**

I have not received any grants, funding or investment for this research project in the last 12 months. My development work so far has been supported on my own time and my own income from my daily work.

If my application is approved, I will update the other funders I might receive in the future and also you.

I hope you can help me, because I find this work very important for the future of Ai use and development within this area.

title: Financial support for NTU AI Safety organizers
creator: 7cf124f1-dfa9-4f15-b7a4-df1b18e27380
description:
### Project summary

As the first AI Safety community in Taiwan, NTU AI Safety has run a reading group for three years. This year, we are scaling our community from 40 to 500+ people. We aim to bridge the gap in AI Safety between Taiwan and the global community. We run reading groups to discuss technical AI Safety techniques and the latest research papers, and we invite professional speakers from organizations such as METR and Anthropic, as well as upcoming AI Safety PhD researchers. We also actively seek partnerships and collaboration opportunities with global AI Safety organizations.

Taiwan has a strong pool of AI research talent and plays an important role in the global AI ecosystem, whether in technical AI research, biomedicine, or hardware. However, there are currently limited formal pathways for people who want to contribute to AI Safety, and not many people are familiar with the field. As the first AI Safety study group in Taiwan, we believe that expanding our community and reaching not only students but also early- and mid-career people is critical to building a stronger pipeline of talent for AI Safety. To ensure the sustainability and continued growth of our organization, we are seeking funding to expand our programs and strengthen our organizational capacity.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

We aim to **help more people understand what AI Safety is, how they can contribute, what potential opportunities are, and how their existing professional expertise can be applied to preventing and mitigating AI risks**. We have observed that while many people are increasingly aware of the potential risks of AI, they often don’t know where to start or how they can contribute. 

We think having an AI Safety community can be an open door for people interested in AI Safety from different backgrounds by helping individuals to be more informed about opportunities and the talent pipeline. It’s also a nice opportunity to build connections with similar values.

Last semester, we organized 2 reading group tracks (Fundamentals and Technical Paper Reading) and 3 speaker events. We had 20 active members (students and working professionals) participating in our reading group and 50 people joining our speaker events. We also established an online presence through Discord, LinkedIn, and our website. We are planning to rerun both tracks.

This semester, we are organizing a 3rd reading group track on AI policy and governance. However, we recognized that there are still relatively few people working on AI policy and governance in Taiwan, after discussing with some members in our reading group with a law background, and we had limited international collaboration or perspectives to bring into the community. 

In addition, there were only four members preparing for the weekly reading group last semester. The workload was heavy and stretched our capacity to the limit.

Therefore, our actions this year

* **Expand the reading group team**: recruit 7 facilitators to share the workload, rotate weekly facilitation, and make the program more sustainable as participation grows.
* **Expand reading group track**: Add AI Governance & Policy track to target law, philosophy, politics, and social science professionals.
* **Reach new communities**: Extend outreach to people from different professional and cause areas who may have relevant expertise or an interest in AI Safety.
* **Build international connections**:  
   * Build an international reading group to connect with universities abroad and explore opportunities for in-person visits and exchange. Potential collaborators include MIT, Oxford, and UChicago.  
   * Collaborate with AI Safety communities across Asia to develop an **AI 2040 for APAC** roadmap.
* **Organize speaker events**: Organize 3–4 speaker events on underexplored AI Safety topics, including international speakers in hardware verification and AI policy, either online or in person.
* **Build cross-sector connection dinner**: Organize connection dinners that bring together students and community members with professors and industry professionals

title: Travel support for an invited PriGM talk at NeurIPS Paris 2026
creator: 223b0b47-6984-491a-a0b4-6952e92e8e92
blurb: USD 2,800 toward travel and accommodation to discuss generative models and inference scaling at PriGM on 12 December.
description:
### 

I am a researcher at MSL FAIR and affiliated with Tel Aviv University, working on the theory of machine learning. I received my PhD in theoretical fundamental physics at Tel Aviv University and then worked as a postdoctoral researcher at EPFL on physics of AI. My research focus centers on how the structure of data interacts with the learning mechanism to shape what models learn, and how that understanding can inform their emergent behaviors, capabilities, alignment and safety at scale.

I am requesting $2,800 to attend NeurIPS Paris, where I have been invited to speak at the Principles of Generative Modeling workshop on December 12, 2026\. I will discuss inference scaling and reasoning models, and also plan to present work with colleagues from Stanford on efficient pass@k sampling for LLM reasoning. The workshop has no budget for my travel or accommodation.

I believe scientific progress depends on researchers exchanging ideas and subjecting them to criticism, and that modern machine learning is an emerging science, lacking much of the methodological honesty of basic sciences (for instance, the meaning of "theory" is subjective, and there is no agreed upon level of "error bars" or reproducibility). This matters particularly in a field developing as quickly as AI, with as big of an impact on the real world. Workshops offer a way for researchers across institutions the opportunity to discuss, find weaknesses in their arguments and create new collaborations. That is the purpose of this trip.

The research direction I want to advance is a deeper understanding of why models behave as they do from a physical perspective, using the simplest models that capture the interesting phenomena. Empirical evaluations can only tell us how a model performs under certain conditions, while understanding the mechanisms underlying that behavior can help us reason about when those results will persist and what are their failure modes, which is particularly crucial for safety and alignment. My work spans the relationship between data structure, learning and inference, including how reasoning models use additional computation, particular with multi-agent swarms and recursive self-improvement, all of which are subjects that will be discussed in the workshop and at NeurIPS in general. I believe this understanding is necessary for building aligned and safe systems that can benefit society.

I employ tools from theoretical physics to study learning and generative models. I have already pursued this direction in multiple papers, and work on these problems every day. The invitation gives me a concrete opportunity to discuss my work with researchers studying complementary aspects of generative modeling. I want to use those discussions to find new interesting questions and build collaborations around them.  
I am particularly interested in collaborating across institutions to tackle the question: _how does the underlying structure of data affect alignment in generative models?_ I believe this is an open question, and my experience shows that the answer can depend on many factors (whether models are just pretrained, RLed, or RLHFed). Building simple models of data that can show where misalignment can emerge and how, and then testing these on real settings would be a very powerful result to come out of this visit.

The planned trip is December 11–15, including four nights in Paris. My current budget is $850 for a return flight, $1,380 for accommodation, a $240 registration fee, $80 for transport, and $250 for food and incidentals, which is approximately $2,800 in total.

Without support, I would pay for the trip personally. This grant would support my participation in an existing scientific program and an opportunity to develop the research relationships surrounding my work.

[PriGM workshop](https://sites.google.com/view/prigmneurips2026/home)

title: Nullivance: Testing Network-Resident State for Multi-Agent AI Safety
creator: 14e1e10b-d6dc-4055-9021-b650f5c6fba0
blurb: A reproducible evaluation of whether a shared network workspace reduces false acceptance in AI oversight
description:
### Project summary

I am requesting support to evaluate Nullivance, a working multi-agent AI network, before its first public release. In many agent systems the effective workspace and memory remain inside each model's context. Nullivance instead keeps goals, evidence, disagreements, permissions, handovers, outcomes, and selected experience in a network-resident operational workspace. An authorized replacement model can enter a defined role and continue from that shared record. Continuity belongs to the network record rather than to a model pretending to remember events it did not witness.

This is useful only if the shared state is trustworthy. Three agents may repeat one unchecked source and make it look like independent confirmation. An agent may report success without verified execution. An unverified outcome may later return as experience and influence a new decision. I want to test whether the Nullivance architecture actually reduces these failures, rather than inferring safety from the complexity of the design.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

I will run a six-month paired evaluation against a strong conventional agent and provenance baseline, matching information, tools, model family, and API cost. Sandboxed tasks will hide execution ground truth from the systems under evaluation and cover three failure families: apparent corroboration from one repeated source; success claims without verified execution; and unverified outcomes re-entering as experience.

Month 1 freezes the threat model, statistical plan, baseline, and stop-or-narrow criteria. Month 2 builds and calibrates the task suite. Months 3 and 4 run paired comparisons, held-out trials, and component ablations. Month 5 is an independent replication and adversarial review. Month 6 resolves findings and publishes the evaluation package. I will preregister the design and publish negative as well as positive results.

How will you know it worked?

The primary metric is false acceptance on runs containing hidden violations. Secondary measures are false rejection, valid-task completion, token and compute cost, and whether an independent human evaluator can reconstruct evidence ancestry, permissions, unresolved disagreements, and actual execution.

A positive result would be a substantial, independently reproduced reduction in false acceptance without achieving it by excessive refusal or cost. A null result would also be useful: if a simpler provenance baseline matches Nullivance, that would redirect work toward cheaper controls. The deliverable is therefore not a claim that my network wins. It is a public, reproducible package containing the protocol, benchmark tasks, baseline, aggregate held-out results, ablations, replication record, and limitations.

How will this funding be used?

The full six-month budget is USD 60,456: researcher stipend including Vietnamese income tax, USD 18,000; research-engineering contractor, USD 13,200; external methods and formal review, USD 7,800; independent replication, USD 5,400; model API ceiling, USD 7,800; compute and evidence storage, USD 2,760; and a 10% contingency of USD 5,496.

A minimum USD 25,000 version would fund a three-month feasibility study: researcher time, protocol and statistical design, a strong baseline, the sandbox task suite, pilot paired runs, and an external methods review. If the proposed distinction has no operational meaning or the baseline matches it, I will stop or narrow the project and report that result. Any API or compute credits received from another source will reduce the corresponding cash line rather than duplicate support.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am Trinh Tung Lam, an independent researcher based in Hanoi, Vietnam. I began the Nullivance research programme in April 2025 and have operated a working network with dated records since August 2026\. I designed its network-resident workspace, role and permission boundaries, controlled artifact exchange, evidence and claim ledgers, handover records, and experience store.

My public nullivance-logic release contains a two-channel propositional logic, a finite-domain quantified extension, two manuscripts, and Lean 4 proof code. Its core soundness and completeness results are machine-checked and sorry-free. Public work: <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21964600> and <https://github.com/lamtung0487-droid/nullivance-logic>.

The operating record includes cases where repeated attestations were refused as independent evidence, conclusions were limited to the exact files inspected, and acceptance was withheld despite 1,150 passing tests because an earlier database interval was unobserved. These are examples of the discipline I want to evaluate independently; they are not yet evidence that Nullivance outperforms a strong baseline.

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The main risks are that the architectural distinction has no measurable effect, the baseline is too weak, the task suite does not represent meaningful failures, the statistical design is underpowered, or an independent reviewer cannot be secured. I will mitigate these by freezing a strong baseline and stop criteria before the main runs, obtaining outside methods review, using held-out trials, preserving hidden ground truth, and publishing counterexamples and null findings.

If the system does not outperform the baseline, I will not present internal component tests as proof of network-level safety. The useful outcome would be a reusable benchmark and a clear account of which additional mechanisms were unnecessary or failed. If the evaluation exposes a serious control or auditability failure, release will be narrowed or delayed.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

USD 0 has been awarded or received. Applications are pending with EA Funds, BlueDot Impact, GTR Foundation, AI Safety Research Fund, CLR Fund, and several providers of API or compute credits, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Together AI, and Principia Labs. I will update this page when any decision is received and will not accept overlapping support for the same costs.

title: Reproducible measurements for a small open-model AI safety evaluation
creator: c811c45e-d735-4a20-a74b-0999368bc6c3
blurb: A three-month pilot to reproduce one open-model safety evaluation, preserving inputs, scoring rules and a fresh-environment replay.
description:
### Project summary

I want to spend three months building the skills and a small public work sample needed to contribute to AI safety evaluation. The output will be a rerunnable evaluation package for one small open model, together with an explanation of the inputs, scoring rules and conditions behind its results.

I propose to run the project from 11 January to 10 April 2027, with the dates adjusted if the funding decision or payment arrives later.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The pilot will use one public evaluation with a documented method and data that can be shared lawfully. I will preserve the model revision, prompts, dataset revision, scoring code, environment and random seeds. After reproducing a baseline, I will vary one evaluation choice at a time and record whether the reported result changes. Failed runs and unresolved discrepancies will remain visible in the package. I will choose the model and task after checking the license, compute requirements and whether I can explain the full evaluation procedure.

* **Weeks 1–4:** Continue Python foundations, complete small data-processing exercises, inspect candidate evaluation licenses and compute needs, and freeze one feasible task and its run specification.
* **Weeks 5–6:** Execute and document a baseline, preserving input versions, commands and outputs.
* **Weeks 7–9:** Vary one evaluation choice at a time, check scoring, and document which comparisons change the result.
* **Weeks 10–12:** Replay from a fresh environment, document remaining discrepancies, request feedback, and release the package and findings.

Reliable measurements matter when people use evaluations to decide which AI systems need further testing or stronger safeguards. This pilot addresses one part of that process: making it possible to inspect how a reported result was obtained and whether it survives a fresh run. I will explain the limits of the selected measurement alongside the findings, so a narrow evaluation is not presented as a general safety judgment.

### How will you know it worked?

By the end, I intend to release a package containing the frozen inputs or lawful retrieval instructions, model and data version identifiers, scoring code, commands and environment information, and the resulting comparison table. The findings note will give the metric and denominator, explain any failed runs, and separate an evaluation-setting effect from a claim about the model's behavior.

I will test the written instructions by rerunning them from a fresh environment. I will seek external feedback, while keeping completion independent of whether a reviewer responds. A fresh self-run will be recorded as a self-run, with any external replay recorded separately.

I will also record which parts of the workflow I can write and explain independently. That record will help determine whether I should continue into evaluation work, deepen my programming foundations, or pursue a more operations-focused contribution to the field.

### How will this funding be used?

The minimum request is $9,000 for a three-month base budget; the $9,900 goal adds a $900 contingency reserve. These are forward-looking budget estimates rather than invoices or documented past expenses. The USD request uses a planning conversion of KRW 1,500 per dollar, rather than claiming a current exchange-rate quote.

* **Time and living support:** $7,000
* **Compute and storage allowance:** $1,000
* **Learning resources:** $200
* **Technical mentoring or review allowance:** $800
* **Base total / minimum funding:** $9,000
* **Contingency reserve:** $900
* **Goal:** $9,900

No mentor or reviewer has been booked. I will avoid buying resources already available to me without added cost. Funding would let me set aside other paid work and concentrate on this transition full-time. I will reconcile overlapping support before accepting funding so the same costs are not funded twice.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am the applicant and would run this pilot myself. My existing work concerns whether a result can be checked against the process that produced it. I am Reproducibility & Evaluation Maintainer for [Throughline](https://github.com/SarthakPattnaik1/throughline-os/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md), an open-source research-software project, with responsibility for replay and evaluation acceptance criteria. My replay-receipt contribution was [merged as PR #52](https://github.com/SarthakPattnaik1/throughline-os/pull/52).

For [TrialTrace](https://github.com/ByungwoongYoo/trialtrace), I designed the record-comparison framework and directed AI-assisted implementation of a local research-record history explorer. I am now learning to write and understand the underlying code directly, beginning with CS50P. This proposal brings those two parts together: experience defining evidence boundaries and a structured period of hands-on technical learning.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The main execution risk is that I do not develop the necessary programming competence quickly enough to complete a model evaluation within the proposed period. At the end of Week 4, I will check whether I can write and explain the basic file-processing, function and test steps required for the selected evaluation. If that gate is not met, I would propose narrowing the work to a documented input-and-scoring audit and seek agreement before making a material funded-scope change.

A second risk is that the selected evaluation needs more compute than the budget allows, or that its data or model cannot be shared under suitable terms. I will screen those requirements before committing to the baseline run. If the experiment produces no meaningful difference between settings, I will still publish the reproducibility package and report that result without presenting it as a new safety finding.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

I have raised $0 in the last 12 months.

I have applied to the Transformative AI Fund for USD 9,900 for overlapping work. I have also applied to BlueDot Rapid for USD 6,600 covering an eight-week version of the same transition. These are alternative funding routes; I would disclose any offers and agree a non-overlapping allocation before accepting support.

title: Evidence Before Done: Check AI agents’ completion claims
creator: aa5f7e2e-f7bc-4b7d-aa89-f574d49cc5e3
blurb: A public toolkit that checks “done” against task results, action evidence and permission boundaries.
description:
### Project summary

I want “done” to mean there is something a person can actually check. Evidence Before Done is a proposed public toolkit for comparing an AI software agent’s completion report with the work it performed and the permissions it was given.

My operating rule is simple: never claim something was built, fixed, tested or deployed unless it actually happened and the evidence supports that claim. I want to turn that requirement into tests other solo builders and small organizations can run.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The first two planning months concentrate the implementation work: define twelve synthetic software tasks with known success criteria and permission boundaries, build an evidence record linking source versions, test results, application state and action receipts, and run repeated comparisons across two available model/agent configurations.

The third month covers validation, error analysis, reproducibility, documentation and public release. I would extend toward thirty scenarios and three configurations only where findings and remaining resources justify it.

The release would include a runnable tool, synthetic examples, instructions and limitations. Existing proprietary business code, customer data and private conversations are outside this public project. This is development work: there is no validated research harness, published result, confirmed partner or recruited user community yet.

How will you know it worked?

The tasks need ground truth defined independently of the agent’s own claims. I would measure unsupported completion claims that the checks catch, failures incorrectly passed, missed failures, repeatability and run cost. A successful project leaves people a usable, reproducible tool and an honest account of where it fails. Negative findings are useful results. This is exploratory oversight tooling; I am not claiming demonstrated prevention of catastrophic AI risk.

How will this funding be used?

The target is $25,000 for three planning months. The minimum is $20,000 for the first two-month phase. If only the minimum is funded, I would deliver a bounded first-phase prototype, initial evaluations and limitations; the third-month expansion and final packaging would require further funding or an explicitly revised scope.

Months 1–2: $12,000 gross individual working stipend for 240 planned hours, $5,000 capped model/API experiments, $1,500 test infrastructure/storage and $1,500 contingency. Total: $20,000.

Month 3: $3,000 gross stipend for 60 planned hours, $1,000 model/API experiments, $500 infrastructure/storage and $500 contingency. Total: $5,000.

The full budget is $15,000 gross stipend, $6,000 experiments, $2,000 infrastructure and $2,000 contingency. Applicant taxes are included in the stipend. These are planning estimates, not incurred costs or vendor quotes. No hiring or outsourcing budget is proposed. Work starts after funding and agreement, with dates adjusted to actual receipt; this cost allocation does not presume a particular payment schedule.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am Avi Mosli, a solo business operator building software with AI assistance. My background includes real estate, hospitality, yacht/marina operations and financial services. I founded a New York brokerage that was later acquired. I hold an A.S. in Mathematics and Computer Science and a B.S. in Land and Energy Management.

I bring requirements about permissions, one source of truth, preserved evidence and visible user outcomes. I do not have an established AI-safety research record or completed results for this proposed tool.

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The checks may miss false claims, accept weak evidence, prove difficult for others to run, or cost too much relative to the benefit. I may also encounter implementation limits as a solo builder. I would report those findings and release usable work and limitations rather than claim the mechanism works. Further expansion depends on what the first phase actually shows.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

No funding has been received for this newly proposed project. Pending overlapping requests include EA Funds/Transformative AI Fund ($25,000), BlueDot Rapid Grants ($5,000), Hacker Initiative ($5,000) and Lightcone Commons ($5,000–$25,000). No award is confirmed. Earlier $5,000 requests used a narrower part-time pilot budget; accepting any award would require scope and budget reconciliation. Every award would be disclosed before accepting overlapping support; no time or cost would be funded twice.

The separate Mozilla GovDog/HollyBot Letter of Intent concerns a different public project. It is not funding for this toolkit.

AI assistance disclosure

AI helped develop and draft this proposal from my operating requirements, organize verified background and project-status facts, and prepare the budget. Its assistance is substantive. The public project is intended to test the mechanism, not assert research results that do not exist.

title: Travel to present our enclave API work at the AI Security Forum
creator: 8800e10a-8d33-411d-ad93-2b23a8989013
blurb: Support my travel to share our Heron fellowship research and get technical feedback on secure access to AI models.
description:
### Project summary

I’m Joel Muigai, a Heron AI Security Fellow based in Nairobi, Kenya. I’m working with Anthony(another fellow) and our mentor Guy who is a member of technical staff at from SL5 on a project we call enclave API. I’m requesting $1,000 to help me attend the Frontier AI Security Forum in Tel Aviv on 22 November and present what we have been working on.

Our project was asks the question below:

How can researchers and their coding agents can run useful experiments on a model without getting direct access to its weights?

We are looking at some of the tasks that researcher run, such as evaluations(evals), mech interp and training workflows (5 primitives). My contribution has been on authentication, job signing approvals and investigating CPU/GPU attestation.

The goals is to make useful research possible while reducing the risk of model weights being stolen or misused. We have a ready prototype, and some gaps we need to test but my presentation will be on progress so far.

### What are this project’s goals? How will you achieve them?

I want to present the team’s design and current experiments, then potentially ask practitioners in the room where our assumptions fail. I’m preparing a short talk with feedback from the team. I will use the forum’s technical discussions and side chats, to get specific criticism that we can turn into changes and improvemenets to our design and evaluation plan.

### How will you know it worked?

I will share the presentation materials and write a short report within two weeks of the event, covering feedback received, unresolved questions and changes we plan to make. The outcome I foresee is concrete suggestions/feedback for tests or design changes.

### How will this funding be used?

This is purely an individual travel request to share our team’s work. The proposed request is $1000\. Heron is funding flights and accommodation capped at $200 per night. However, Visa acquisition fees, Food and transportation in Israel will not be covered. This funds will go into covering those expenses both here in Kenya and in Israel. Below is the cost breakdown

Estimated Budget:

Visa, photos and supporting documents: $100

Meals not provided by organisers: $200

Airport transfers and local transport in Kenya and Israel: $250

Travel insurance: $100

Mobile data(roaming): $150

Reserve for price changes or travel disruption: $200

### Who is on your team? What’s your track record on similar projects?

The enclave API is shared team work within the Heron fellowship. Anthony and I work on the implementation with guidance from Guy who is a member of the technical staff at Sl5\. I have worked on Hardware security before under the guidance of Jonathan Happel as part of SPAR. This project is distinct in execution although some concepts overlap. For this project, I designed and implemented researcher authentication and signed job approvals, including a live Google Cloud KMS signing experiment. My work focused on carrying authorization through to execution, then testing rejection of altered or unauthorized requests, and investigating CPU/GPU attestation.

Our code and experiments: [Enclave API repository](https://github.com/Heron-AI-Security/enclave-api).

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The main risks are visa delays or travel disruption preventing me from attending, or discussions at the forum producing limited actionable feedback. I would prepare specific questions and arrange relevant conversations beforehand. If I cannot attend, I would share our presentation remotely and seek feedback through Heron.
