title: FlowSight: an Open Small Model for User-Controlled Work Assistance
creator: dcd9dff1-288e-427f-9188-ccec63b511bb
blurb: A first reusable model/adaptation, local reference workflow and honest task/resource evaluation.
description:
Project summary

I am Manuel Castillejo Vela, a technical founder in Seville, Spain. With CTO Eduardo Robles Russo, I build FlowSight, a desktop workspace that uses local AI to help people recover work context and prepare useful summaries. We want to develop and release a first compact, task-specific open model/adaptation, with a local reference workflow and reproducible evaluation. Our own model has not yet been trained; the working app currently uses a third-party Qwen3-VL-2B model locally.

This grant would support public research and reusable outputs, available without purchasing FlowSight. It would not buy our private application code or subsidize marketing. The goal is to learn when small local models can provide useful assistance while keeping people in control, and to publish the evidence and limitations. We do not claim that local AI is always more efficient or already delivers carbon savings.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Over ten weeks after funding, we would select a compact, license-compatible baseline and a bounded training or adaptation approach for editable work summaries. We would prepare artificial or explicitly permitted examples, record their provenance and separate training from evaluation. We would release the resulting model or adaptation, the relevant training/reference code, an evaluation set we have rights to publish, a model card and English/Spanish documentation under appropriate open licenses compatible with any upstream assets.

Weeks 1-2: define the task, reuse rights, baselines, evaluation protocol and compute budget. Weeks 3-6: implement and train/adapt a first candidate, logging the training configuration and resource use. Weeks 7-8: evaluate task quality, unsupported statements, instruction following, user-control boundaries, latency and memory on available desktop hardware. Weeks 9-10: obtain an independent review and publish a reproducible release, results and limits. Hardware electricity measurements would be reported only where we have reliable equipment; whole-system environmental impacts would not be inferred from partial measurements.

How will you know it worked?

Success means a downloadable first task-specific model/adaptation, a reference that runs locally, reproducible public tests, documented data/model provenance and a report that compares the candidate against the chosen baseline. We would report errors alongside performance. If adaptation does not improve useful task quality, we would publish that negative result and the tools rather than claim success. Training compute, unsupported hardware, privacy limits and evaluation weaknesses would be visible. We have not measured these outcomes yet.

How will this funding be used?

The maximum request is USD10,000: USD8,000 for 160 hours of model, reference and evaluation engineering at an indicative USD50/hour; USD1,000 for a capped training/compute budget; USD1,000 for independently contracted evaluation and release review, with the reviewer recruited after an award. No reviewer is already engaged. This is a scoped first release, not a budget to train a large foundation model from scratch.

At the USD5,000 minimum, we would reduce engineering to 80 hours/USD4,000, compute to USD500 and independent review to USD500\. The smaller version would prioritize a license-compatible adaptation, local reference and fewer clearly documented test cases. No hardware purchases or paid growth are included. Actual supplier/compute choices would be made within the award and rights constraints; funds would be used for the agreed public outputs.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Manuel Castillejo Vela is FlowSight Founder/CEO and a technical builder; Eduardo Robles Russo is CTO and a software engineer. Both work full-time in Seville and met as Software Engineering classmates. FlowSight operates through Manuel's Spanish sole-proprietor registration, dated 1 September 2026; a separate company has not yet been incorporated. Development began in 2025, with a public product launch in February 2026\. We estimate 50-100 users in Spain and China; this is a founder estimate, not a measured monthly-active-user count. Revenue is zero. Existing local-inference experience supports the proposed engineering, but does not establish experience training a new foundation model.

Product: https://flowsight.site

Manuel: https://www.linkedin.com/in/manuel-castillejo-vela/

Eduardo: https://www.linkedin.com/in/eduardo-robles-russo-5133912b1

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The baseline may be unsuitable, a compact model may not be accurate enough, adaptation may exceed the compute budget, or useful examples may lack clear release rights. We would narrow the task, cap spending and publish permitted code, tests and negative findings. We would not release data without rights or represent an upstream model as our original training. Broad adoption and reduced dependence on central inference are goals, not guaranteed outcomes. The open research outputs would remain usable independently of the commercial app.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

We have received no external investment or cash grants. Programme memberships and recognitions are not cash funding. SECURE, FUTO, GitHub Secure Open Source Fund, Awesome Disability and the two initial Mozilla applications are pending. A separate USD1,000 Awesome Conservation and Climate application was just received for measurement equipment for a new public electricity experiment; no award is granted. There is also a proposed private fundraising round, not committed capital.

The Mozilla model/research proposals and this request are alternative routes wherever their scope overlaps. If more than one funder offers support, we would disclose it and resolve scopes before accepting awards; the same hours, compute and deliverables would not be charged twice. Any equipment funded by the climate proposal would not be billed here. A separate behavioral-safety pilot may also be submitted as alternative funding for overlapping evaluation work. All awards remain uncertain.

AI assistance was used to organize and translate my previously supplied project and personal information and this grant plan. I have not represented this as unaided human writing. This proposal describes planned work, not completed research.

title: SafeLoadAI: covering whole LLM04 gap in OWASP TOP 10
creator: efc4a057-0b02-4cf4-b8bd-00beef5a3249
description:
**Project summary**

**SafeLoadAI is a python library that prevents RCE coming from insecure deserialization - what it does is scanning AI model files, using both static and dynamic analysis and checking whether the file is malicious or not. If so, it prevents loading. However, it does not currently detect any backdoored or poisoned model weights.**

**What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?**

**I aim to cover LLM04 from OWASP TOP 10 LLM - detection of backdoored and poisoned model weights, so the goal is to create a LLM03/LLM04-covering tool that is robust.**

**I will achieve this in two phases:**

**\- cheching whether the hash matches any of known malicious files**

**\- comparing the weights with other well known, open source models**

**How will you know it worked?**

**I will conduct several tests including variety of known cyber attacks based on both poisoning weights and using backdoors.**

**How will this funding be used?**

**\- API costs (code development, conducting tests, research)**

**\- Computing costs (experiments, generation of new test data)**

**Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?**

**I work alone, it's my idea. SafeLoadAI is already a working project, published on PyPI. It was tested with around 5000 files, and reached detection rate of malicious model files around 98% ( while using --malicious-only mode - without it, it has 15% of FP and 100% TP)**

**What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?**

**The most likely causes of failure are zero-day attacks — the tool may miss new backdoor techniques it hasn’t been built to recognize — and the outcome is successful evasion - user believes he is protected by scanner. At the project level, the main risk is that weight-diffing (phase 2) turns out too noisy to reliably distinguish malicious tampering from legitimate fine-tuning.**

**How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?**

**I haven't raised any money yet**

title: Prove: Cryptographically Sealed AI Benchmark Evaluations & Drift Observatory
creator: 31154356-a488-4e86-816a-e30c2d1778b5
blurb: Open-source pre-registration and Bitcoin OpenTimestamps attestation to eliminate benchmark gaming, data contamination, and silent model drift.
description:
**Project summary**

TriplePass Labs is building Prove, an open source evaluation protocol and command-line interface that cryptographically seals benchmark evaluation runs into Bitcoin block headers using OpenTimestamps. Now benchmark leaderboards are not trustworthy. They are vulnerable to model drift prompt over-tuning and retroactive cherry picking. Prove gives cryptographic receipts. These receipts prove that a specific evaluation was run on a model version at a specific time and only at that time. There is no way to tamper with the results afterward. At the time we are developing Colony Zero. This is a research testbed to see if a swarm of smaller models—like three 8-billion-parameter models or four 14-billion-parameter models—can match or beat a single large frontier model. The goal is to do this under compute and token parity.

**What are the projects objectives? How are you going to achieve them?**

1\. Ship Prove v1.0 CLI: We will. Release a command-line tool that allows users to automatically register evaluation manifests before they run (prove pre-register) and then seal them into Bitcoin using OpenTimestamps (prove seal --anchor ots). Once an evaluation finishes the execution merkle tree gets sealed directly into the Bitcoin blockchain. Auditors can verify these receipts offline in milliseconds. They don’t need to trust TriplePass Labs or any third party to confirm the result.

2\. Launch the Public Agent Drift Observatory: We will deploy an automated testing system that runs evaluation sweeps every day and every week across than ten frontier APIs and open-weight models. We will track model capability drift over time. Publish our findings publicly.

3\. Advance the Colony Zero Swarm benchmarks: We will expand our existing benchmark dataset. This dataset compares -agent swarms with large monolithic reasoning systems. We will ensure both are under compute and token equality. We will release all the proofs and data openly.

**How will you know its worked?**

\- Metric 1: We release the Prove Python package on PyPI. It will include OpenTimestamps anchoring and verification features. It will pass all automated test suites with 100% offline proof verification working

\- Metric 2: The Agent Drift Observatory web dashboard goes live. It will index least 100 sealed evaluation runs anchored into Bitcoin block headers. Each run will have a merkle proof.

\- Metric 3: We release a Colony Zero swarm benchmark report. The report will include -registered manifests and open datasets on Hugging Face.

\- Metric 4: At least three independent AI safety researchers or external benchmark maintainers start using Prove to attest their evaluations.

**How will the funding be utilised?**

We are asking for $15,000 to fund a six-month execution sprint. We will achieve a viable milestone with just $5,000:

\- Dedicated Local Evaluation Rig ($4,500): A 24/7 evaluation rig with high-VRAM GPUs. This allows us to run open-weight models locally with no metered runtime and ensures results.

\- High Speed NVMe storage & dedicated Bitcoin node ($2,000): Fast IOPS storage for raw execution traces and a Bitcoin node that always verifies block headers.

\- Multi-Model Cloud & API Inference ($4,500): A six-month budget for running inference across frontier models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, Gemini) and decentralised open-weight GPU endpoints for continuous drift monitoring.

\- Public Drift. Web Hosting ($2,000): Cloud hosting for the dashboard proof verification explorer and telemetry database.

\- Educational Research Media ($2,000): We will produce audio, video and open technical documentation. These will be released on YouTube to help researchers learn about evaluation pipelines.

**Who's on your team? What's your track record on projects?**

Christopher Ayers is the founder of TriplePass Labs LLC, based in Puyallup, WA. He is an analytics systems architect with 15 years of experience building large-scale data and operational pipelines in enterprise environments. Over the year he has focused on AI systems integration, cryptographic attestation and empirical multi-agent evaluation. He built the core architecture of Prove. Has a fully deployed interactive Colony Zero explorer on Hugging Face Spaces. He works on TriplePass Labs for 8 to 12 hours per week at night and on weekends while also working full time in analytics.

**What are the probable causes of failure and what would be the likely consequences if this project did fail?**

\- Cause 1: Lack of community adoption. If benchmark authors think cryptographic pre-registration adds any workflow friction Prove might remain a niche tool. Mitigation: We are building Prove with zero-friction CLI wrappers. These will work as add-ons to existing tools like Inspect AI and lm-evaluation-harness. Just add one flag: --anchor ots.

\- Cause 2: Hardware or API cost overruns. If API prices go up sharply or local testing hits bottlenecks continuous drift sweeps could get throttled. Mitigation: We will focus more on open-weight models. We will use backoff on API polling and cap frequency on stable benchmarks.

\- If the project fails, with slow industry adoption, the full protocol OpenTimestamps verification libraries and the Colony Zero swarm evaluation dataset will all be fully open sourced under Apache 2.0 and MIT licenses. This ensures lasting value, for the source AI safety research community.

**How much have you raised in the 12 months and from where?**

TriplePass Labs LLC is a brand company, formed in October 2026\. It is 100% self-funded. To date we have raised $0 in funding. We have no venture capital, no debt and no dilutive equity. We are currently applying for -dilutive grants (Emergent Ventures, Solo Grants SFF Speculation Grants) but we have not received any disbursements yet.

title: MedScale: Open-Source Security and Synthetic FHIR Verification
creator: ec3a1e78-eabc-40d0-8c2c-3a2bfb96c17c
blurb: A free, local-first Apache-2.0 health AI project; support independent privacy testing, security review, and developer hardware.
description:
Project summary

MedScale is an existing, independently maintained, free Apache-2.0 local-first desktop health AI project with FHIR-native workflows and Windows/macOS engineering-beta builds. Its public code and project information are at <https://github.com/AbdulazizShehri/MedScale> and <https://medscale.si/>. The project is not clinically certified, and the engineering tests described here use fictional/synthetic data only. I am seeking voluntary grant funding to make the software more trustworthy and maintainable, not to introduce paywalls.

Goals and approach

Over a proposed six-month funding period, I aim to:

1\. Expand the reproducible, synthetic-only FHIR evidence-attribution, abstention, privacy and reliability test suite; publish methods and results that other developers can run independently.

2\. Obtain an independent external security review and publish a responsible summary and remediation evidence without disclosing unpatched weaknesses.

3\. Improve Windows/macOS build and regression testing, documentation, and offline-first usability, with a particular focus on devices available to independent maintainers.

4\. Publish regular progress updates, transparent limitations, and an openly accessible reproducibility guide. These are intended deliverables, not completed or promised clinical outcomes.

What success would look like

A public Apache-2.0 testing harness and synthetic fixtures; repeatable scripts and reports; an independently reviewed security improvement plan and evidence of fixes; tested Windows/macOS engineering builds and a documented maintenance process. The results will be measured by reproducible pass/fail cases, verified code changes and publicly reviewable artifacts, not by unverified patient usage or medical effectiveness.

How funding would be used

The full proposed funding goal of $25,000 USD is a planning budget: $10,000 for maintainer engineering time, $7,500 for an independent security assessment and verification, $5,000 for development/test hardware, and $2,500 for documentation, accessibility and reproducibility testing. Quotes and actual vendors would be selected transparently after funding; they are not signed contracts. If only the $5,000 minimum is raised, I would reduce scope to a documented synthetic evaluation and a bounded independent security review, and not promise full delivery of all milestones. Funding will be used only for public-benefit open-source work, not for patient data or paid clinical services. No expense will be double-charged against any other grant.

Team and track record

This is currently an independent maintainer-led project. I have an MPH from the University of Melbourne, an AWS certification, and I maintain public MedScale code, build/test documentation and engineering-beta artifacts. The repository is the best evidence of prior work. I am not claiming institutional sponsorship, a clinical deployment, patient adoption, or a named external reviewer who has not agreed to participate.

Risks, limits and transparency

Risks include hardware availability, time needed for security review, dependency vulnerabilities, compatibility issues, and a limited maintainer capacity. If funding is lower than hoped, I will narrow milestones, report the actual results and remaining gaps, and follow the eventual grant agreement for any unspent funds. The public project remains free and independently controlled. No health records from real patients will be used in the grant work.

Existing funding

No cash grant, device shipment, or GPU allocation has been confirmed for MedScale at the time of posting. Other grant inquiries and applications are pending; this proposal does not count them as money received. If more than one funder supports the work, separate cost accounting will prevent double funding.

Writing disclosure

This factual proposal was organized with AI-assisted drafting; the maintainer is responsible for verifying the project description, budget assumptions and deliverables.

title: Our Own Research Archive - Open, free and accessible science
creator: 16475ce9-74db-4969-8f2f-0345c7481b15
blurb: 500 foundational works across subjects released as responsive HTML, an open source golang framework that just works, and infra that maintains itself further
description:
### Project summary

![](https://fkousziwzbnkdkldjper.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/image-uploads/92ead083-3794-f8ff-68ca-a14a435b6b14)![](https://fkousziwzbnkdkldjper.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/image-uploads/7030b788-84e9-ff67-62ec-5ab482254244)![](https://fkousziwzbnkdkldjper.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/image-uploads/1d750342-58fb-f3b6-d672-37858f70cf5c)

In 3rd century BCE, there goes the legend of a scholar who stared in the eyes of the lord to say "_A flaw is a flaw, even if you open your third eye,"_ calling out a factual error even if you are the god. While the king stands perplexed between bowing to the lord, but not daring the scholar to calm down.

![](https://fkousziwzbnkdkldjper.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/image-uploads/bf9b026d-dfa4-a0de-78c7-9bc31c3f5745)

The scholars were never the ones to bow down to anything. Journals were meant as a curated collections with the particular vision, for easier reading and follow through.  
  
But today:  
\- Public tax and grants fund the research work  
\- Researchers do research on their subject and create breakthroughs  
\- Researchers then spend months in the submission cycle for every single journal they want to attempt to, because you cannot publish one paper to be included in two journals (Imagine if someone said one song can only be in person's playlist and no other?)  
\- Other researchers spend their time reviewing the draft for free  
\- They tell you, your work is accepted to their journal  
\- So after doing the work, you also pay in thousands of dollars to sign over your copyright, you bundle it into 2 column 8pt layout that got it's culture from 17th century when you had to save space, except it's digital now and still hasn't changed after centuries.   
\- Your institution either pays millions of dollars to read and access the work they funded.  
\- Oh you want it without a subscription? Pay $48 for 24 hours access to this specific article. For the work your fellow colleague did.  
  
and that's assuming your paper fits that specific human committee's vision of what the field should read.   
  
If your paper is slightly outside of any of the conditions laid out even if it's world changing? Nope for journals. If it's Math/CS/.., you could probably try Arxiv. But any moment it fails to be captured in just 2-3 fields because it applies methods used in one field, theory of another, and experimenting routines of 3rd (even if it's how the best discoveries and inventions are made) ? Nope.  
  
That's what academic journal wheel tells everyone.   
  
What do you do? Dump it as a pdf in a format that's expected into any of the servers that serve PDF, and let's not even start about their discoverability.  
  
Back in mid to late 2000's, fan made stories also called fanfictions, were forming a community. You write and submit it to [fanfiction.net](http://fanfiction.net) or similar app, guess what they did? deleted thousands of works overnight without notice of what they considered as bad or good, deleted any works that could offend the advertisers, and thousands of fans lost hundreds of thousands of words of writing. It's either their curated collection, which holds every right over your life's work and can delete them at whim  
  
...sounds eerily familiar? Yup, same problem as current research distribution.  
  
Guess what they did? Fans came together to create "Archive of our own" (AO3) - a non profit, non commercial archive by and for fans to host their works without the overlords, with one goal:  
  
Make a work findable to someone to who wants it by...letting them search for it. Yes, not a fancy algorithm, but literally lets you do  
  
Fandom: `Harry potter, Lord of rings` Include: `Time travel, Chamber of Secrets` Exclude: `Mature Scenes`  
  
Oh yes,  
Field: `Biotechnology, Biology`, Include: `Protein Folds, Negative Results`, Exclude: `Survey Papers`   
  
See? It's been 17 years that day, and now has hosted over 18.4 million works. You get it. (If you don't it's okay, please feel free to drop your doubts in comments and I will be happy to explain : )

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The codebase of AO3 is open source. But it was built in 2008-09 when Ruby on Rails were the gold standard for web frameworks, and we have come a long way since then.  
  
Adopting a system is taking the best parts of it (architecture) and leaving the baggage that comes with that history (Ruby, Elastic search is a an absolute hoarder), and implementing it through what's gold standard today.  
  
Everything in rust would give the best performance, but not so much in long term maintenance. So, we are going with golang - accessible enough language for the community to learn but performant enough for sustainability.   
  
There comes our goals:  
\- Full feature parity (as appropriate, leaving out fandom specific quirks) golang port becomes OORA - Our Own Research Archive  
\- A server side rendering golang framework strong enough to hold the logic of AO3, also open sourced for the wider community, so it's useful beyond this immediate project. (See [cozy-mug](https://github.com/lalithaar/cozy-mug) for current progress) to support projects built in resource constrained environments, so you don't have to choose between performance, accessibility, and minimal resource usage.  
\- Allow researchers; to post their works freely, write in markdown, HTML first with PDF Download support, built in search engine optimization, along with choice to consent to AI reading it vs training in it.  
\- Release foundational works across the fields in the same format to make science accessible, even if retrospectively. Further funds will help increase the coverage of these works in CC by or public domains.  
\- Give back journal curation to scholars. Anyone with their team can can form a thesis to create a journal on, and community kudos support it.  
\- Researchers wake up to kudos and bookmarks of their works, rather than just 1-2 citations now and then.  
You may ask, but Lalitha how are you even going to scrape and format all those papers? I plan to expand upon the CAAS framework (Constrained AI-Assisted Sampling for Fragmented Textual Spaces: <https://isrl-research.github.io/pub/2026-04-m-caas/>) I used to tackle the last project (also converged with Google Research independently on global flood data.) for agentic workflows,   
  
But grounding it through taxonomy, and guidelines that's not just mark down files, so it doesn't go into existential crisis over a single confusion that could have been resolved with a single yes or no from the user, thereby wasting tons of tokens.

### How will you know it worked?

\- Golang framework developed enough for alpha  
\- 50 foundational papers in accessible HTML, indexed in google.  
  
Here's the deal, I know it is only the best case that everyone finds their place and it becomes the new standard, I know the probability is low.  
  
**But here's the worst case:** 50+ foundational works across subject matters turned into fully accessible responsive html that can be indexed in google, and filtered by exactly what you want to look for. An SSR framework in golang that is strong enough to host the scale - open sourced so people working in resource constrained environments can whip up a project 0-1 without sacrificing the performance go language offers. A free space for people to host their works, and each funding bringing down the costs needed to add further papers compounding down.

### How will this funding be used?

**First $8500**  
\- $6000 Stipend to cover 1 month of full time work  
\- $1000 My current laptop was given by my university then to support my work, but it cannot handle the heavy load needed for the python libraries (`marker pdf`) and parsers needed. This will let me setup a desktop workstation, so that I can finally return my laptop back to university where current freshers who would need it can utilise it.  
\- $500 Server (Looking into Hetzner CAX21) along with backup, image transformation and misc costs for 2 years  
\- $1000 AI credits (Gemini/Kimi was the best fit from the initial experiments, will test others if needed).   
**This will enable:**   
\- Release 50 foundational works across subjects in responsive HTML in the web instead of it being stuck in PDF's.  
\- Give researchers a place to publish their works with proper in site search, along with SEO built in. They don't have to worry about formatting and can write in markdown. Control over whether it can be cited by AI, and also if it can be used for training purposes (through robots.txt support per work).  
\- Running server for 2 years to ensure the work remains active.   
\- Covers core Capital expenditures, so every further fund focuses on Operational expenditures and releasing more and more papers.  
\- Alpha Release of SSR Golang framework that just works.  
  
**Every $7000 from here on:**  
\- $6000 Stipend to cover 1 month of full time work  
\- $1000 in AI credits  
**This will enable:**   
\- Support further development of the go lang framework  
\- Maintenance and support for OORA application  
\- Research, catalogue and discover more works with open licenses  
\- Produce OORA versions of the works  
\- Support proper tagging, and tag wrangling of the new works added.  
\- Estimated 300 works per month.  
\- Further development of the architecture/pipeline used in this process to reduce costs per paper the more papers we add.  
  
**Every $23 beyond first $8.5k releases one more foundational work in OORA. So every bit counts : )**  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I will be working on this solo, while consulting Subject Matter Experts for any doubts that may arise during tag creations in the respective fields.   
  
In the last year, I led an [open research lab](https://isrl-research.github.io/). It started with a computer saying instant noodles is healthier than rice and as an advocate for non violence, I didn't want it to be beaten by every grandma in the area. So I went down a 9 month rabbit hole that [produced 9 works](https://isrl.in/google-scholar-if-it-worked/), all open source with 3,813 reads, 1,780 downloads,  
  
It was [process ](https://github.com/isrl-research/sandbox-research/discussions/4)open, not just outputs.   
  
Developed the E-M-F Tri-Axial Model for ingredient identity, transformation, and function: a method informed by S. R. Ranganathan's Colon Classification, a century of Supreme Court precedents, ITC-HSN codes, and FSSAI rulesets.  
  
It is the first method to apply NOVA processing deterministically at the ingredient level, trained undergraduate researchers to move from basic research practice to multi-jurisdiction legal analysis in four weeks.  
  
We produced an [allergen ](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19877561)report that compared the regulations regarding food allergens across 5 jurisdictions along with reconciling it with what the medical literature said.  
  
It was reviewed by an expert who spent his career on studying food allergens in India, and his comment was “It has come out well. Very few comments”.

We planned to submit the work to a journal but also push it to a preprint server. Then came the task that was tougher than producing the work itself: finding a journal.  
  
No, this didn't have a generalised global report because the problem at hand was for India. Submitting it to a global journal meant toning down everything that was India specific about it, that is trying to pose infant food as adult food and vice versa.  
  
We tried Indian journals, but all of them meant we must not push it to an open server or internet at any level and must be in their format however inaccessible.  
  
I [paused ](https://isrl.in/pausing-isrl-respecting-the-work-supporters-and-oneself/)the project few months later to protect the integrity of the work, because despite all the work, the first doubt wasn’t about a methodology we used, or how it can be generalized, but rather that of the legitimacy of the work and which huge institution is doing the work to deserve/receive support and funding.  
  
The second doubt was, why is it not published in an international Q1 journal (Even if that would mean watering down the reports to fit the journal’s vision and to generalize it so it’s not ‘only for India’ but widely applicable. In a work, that is specifically for India.)  
  
That was an open question I had in mind since then, where is the space for works that don't fit the specific academic silo a particular journal expects? That publishing a non silo'd work in the open without paying $8000 shouldn't mean the work being inaccessible, un-indexed, skepticism at every stance instead of rational judgement of the work.  
  
Few months later is when I got a direction on how we can tackle this, cue OORA.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

\- Agentic workflows not being strong enough to cleanly port the papers, but we still have the fallback of existing agentic system even if the experiment to bring down the costs fail  
\- Feature bloat. I plan to tackle this by only adding the core features needed for it to be functional, and nothing more. AO3's codebase will also help me anchor this in the heuristic.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

50K INR (\~$528 USD) for the open research lab I said about, from FOSS United Foundation through Nagarathna Memorial Grant.

title: Travel support grant to present our paper at GigaNet and UN’s IGF
creator: 6c514c5e-370c-4352-97a1-11e6fa6b864b
description:
### Project summary

We are a three person early-career research team seeking travel funding to present our paper at GigaNet Annual Symposium and give a lightning talk at UN’s Internet Governance Forum (IGF) from 14-18 December 2026 in Nairobi, Kenya. 

Our paper introduces a three-dimensional index for scoring multilateral AI governance frameworks on concentration, reversibility and efficiency. We applied the index to five frameworks and identified that the existing frameworks are fragmented and lack a combination of low concentration, medium reversibility and high efficiency. The index is live at <https://governance-index.camilla-balbis.workers.dev/>  

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

International AI governance is fragmenting into overlapping frameworks that trade efficiency for concentrated power or disperse power at the cost of effectiveness.The current frameworks lack a combination of low concentration, medium reversibility, and high efficiency. Our project develops a three-dimensional index to map where each framework sits on this design space and identifies the institutional levers that shift a framework's position along each dimension. Our proposals were accepted by the MAG (Multistakeholder Advisory Group) for the IGF lightning talk, and by the reviewers of the GigaNet symposium. Two of the three team members will travel to Nairobi to present our work at both the GigaNet session and IGF’s lightning talk. We have the following goals-

1\. Present our paper at the GigaNet symposium.

2\. Give a 20 minute lightning talk at IGF.

3\. Build relationships with participants including researchers and practitioners working on multilateral AI governance, UN agency staff and policymakers. 

4\. The intended long-term impact is better-designed international AI governance during the current formative period, reducing the risk of governance failures during transformative AI transitions. 
  
  
### How will you know it worked?

Our team met through Mangrove, and we got feedback from the ecosystem.

Immediate measurable outputs-

1. GigaNet paper presented on 14th december.
2. Lightning talk delivered on the main IGF program.
3. Paper publication and addition to GigaNet proceedings.
4. At least 10 substantive conversations with target researchers and practitioners.

Projected long-term outcomes-

1. Citations of the paper or index by AI governance researchers.
2. Use of the index as a tool by third parties.
3. Invitations to extend the work through follow-up collabs and/or workshops.

### How will this funding be used?

 The funds would be used for travelling to attend the event for two out of three team members. The following is the rough estimate-

1. Round trip flights x 2: approx $900 and $950.
2. Shared accommodation in Nairobi (to reduce cost)- approx $125
3. IGF registration and accreditation- free
4. Local transport, food, visas and insurance- covered by the team
5. Miscellaneous expense/price fluctuations- $25  
Total- $2000

For detailed break-through refer to the following sheet-

<https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L7GF4mxOY0Rexg4XKjOfdP0QUUJ4c2%5FmVZq48%5F53TZw/edit?usp=sharing>  
  
### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

The team was built through [Mangrove](https://try.mangrove.one). Our team consists of-

1. Camilla Balbis (Canada) is SPAR Fellow, ML4Good Alumni, judge and panelist for 3 Apart Research Hackathons, AIGS Canada paper on AI preparedness and BlueDot course facilitator and mentor <https://www.linkedin.com/in/camillabalbis/>
2. Jeanne Marie Vincendeau (France) is dual Master’s in International Relations between LUISS (Rome) and CFAU (Beijing) magna cum laude, mentor and facilitator for 3 AI safety fellowships, namely Mercial, AIxBio Africa and Nous. <https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeanne-vincendeau/>
3. Parveen Sheikh (India) is an interdisciplinary researcher with a Masters’s in Social Exclusion and Inclusive policy, founder of NISA and former policy researcher for the Indian Parliament. <https://www.linkedin.com/in/parveen-sheikh/>

Jeanne and Parveen will travel to Nairobi and Camilla will contribute to the presentation virtually. 

Track record on this project- peer-reviewed acceptance at the GigaNet Annual symposium 2026 and an online published live index tool. <https://governance-index.camilla-balbis.workers.dev/>

Lighting talk details: <https://intgovforum.org/en/content/igf-2026-lightning-talk-40-discussing-global-ai-governance-and-power-concentration>  
  
### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The most likely cause would be funding shortage to present our work. If we cannot fund this trip then we would have to forgo the opportunity to share our work and to engage with the IGF and its UN connected network of practitioners and decision-makers. The paper and the index exist regardless, the only counterfactual loss is the network-building and the two speaking slots. 

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

As a team, this is our first attempt at raising money. All the work we have done has been on a volunteer basis.

title: Benchmark Reporting Census: a public record of what labs choose to report
creator: 0b29411b-4814-4b25-86ec-93d9e5795a82
blurb: A frozen public census of which AI benchmarks frontier labs choose to report, so selective reporting cannot hide.
description:
### Project summary

A frozen, public census of which benchmarks frontier labs report, so researchers and policymakers can see selective reporting and benchmark saturation over time.

Benchmark Radar is a live, public database and search engine for AI benchmarks and evaluations, with 42,745+ records gathered from public sources and updated daily. It is already used and cited: an arXiv paper (arXiv:2609.11115), a public Hugging Face dataset, a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.22167102), and a Hugging Face #1 Paper of the Day.

The new deliverable is a reporting census. For each major benchmark, the census records how many frontier lab model reports and model cards included it in each release period, starting with every frontier model report from January 2024 to December 2026\. Call this reporting prevalence. The census does not claim a benchmark is valid, and it does not claim to know what a lab runs internally. It records only what labs choose to publish.

No single model card can show two things. First, a lab quietly dropping a dangerous-capability evaluation that appeared in last year's model card and is missing from this year's. Second, a benchmark that is saturated or contaminated still being cited as evidence of progress. Only the comparison across many reports and many periods shows either pattern, and today nobody keeps that comparison in a frozen, citable form. A public census gives researchers, auditors, and policymakers a shared record that cannot be quietly edited after the fact, because each release is frozen with a DOI.

  
### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Deliverable: Census v1, covering frontier model reports from January 2024 to December 2026, frozen with a Zenodo DOI, by month 3 after funding. After v1, the census updates with each new frontier model release, and the underlying data stays public in the Radar dataset.

  
### How will you know it worked?

Success is measured by: v1 shipped on schedule with its DOI; independent citations and reuse of the census data; continued updates after each frontier release. Kill criterion: if the census has zero independent citations by month 9, I stop and write up what was learned instead of continuing.

  
### How will this funding be used?

The budget is mostly my time. My time: $6,500 per month (a US postdoc-level rate: above the NIH postdoc stipend floor of $5,290/month and below the roughly $6,900/month equivalent paid to MATS fellows, neither of which is a like-for-like comparison because those come with employer benefits or housing and meals, and this budget provides none). Census v1 is 3 months of my time: $19,500\. API and compute for report collection and extraction: $4,000\. Infrastructure, hosting, storage for a year: $1,000\. Census v1 total: $24,500\. Full program: $50,000 (Census v1 $24,500, plus $25,500 for citation-tracking tooling and 12 months of census updates at part-time effort across the year). The paid period starts with my OPT in early 2027; I am an F-1 student until graduation in December 2026 and cannot be paid personally for this work before then.

  
### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Koutian Wu, solo. I built Benchmark Radar solo and maintain it daily. Lead author of the Benchmark Radar paper and of a first-author NeurIPS 2026 workshop paper on provenance in AI-assisted research (arXiv:2610.28655). Core contributor to Apex ASI-Bench (task and scorer validity). Contributor to Petri, the alignment auditing tool, with two tested upstream fixes landed. I evaluate AI models for research at UT Austin, where I finish an M.S. in AI for Sciences in December 2026\. Links: https://benchmark-radar.org, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11115, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22167102.

  
### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

Reporting data is incomplete by nature: some labs publish thin model cards, and the census records absence of reporting, not absence of testing; the write-ups will say this plainly. My immigration status limits how grant money can be paid to me personally before my OPT begins in 2027, so the paid period is set to start with OPT, and I am confirming the arrangement with my international office before funds move.

  
### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

None raised in the last 12 months. Grant applications are pending with BlueDot Impact Fund, the Transformative AI Fund, and Lightcone Commons, submitted November 2026; no decisions or funds received yet.

title: Independent AI safety research program: interpretability and agentic evals
creator: 463cec36-0e2b-4120-afd8-bcd8b617ba32
blurb: Twelve months of compute, model access and research time for a pre-registered interpretability study, a self-preservation eval, and the ideas that follow them
description:
### Project summary

I am applying for twelve months of funding for my independent AI safety research as a whole program, rather than for a single study. The money would pay for three things: GPU compute for training models and working with their activations, API access to models from several providers so that I can run evaluations across them, and the coding assistants I use to build and run my experiments.

Two safety projects lead the program, and both are already running and producing results. The first is a pre-registered study of the geometry that training on reasoning traces builds inside a model; the second is an agentic evaluation of self-preservation behaviour. I keep a record of every project, run and change of plan in my Research Ledger, and every project named here can be read without an account at <https://ledger.listentomarcus.org/v/uk95-3nyx-gkfg> 

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Most of my projects ask what training changes inside a model, and answer it with the same decoding and similarity methods I used on EEG data.

**The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Distillation (RL-D1ST).** Does training on reasoning traces build a shared, transferable geometry of planning states, in base, instruct and R1-distilled Llama-3.1-8B? The study has run 13 stages. Its pre-registered causal test failed for a diagnosable reason: the random null removed far more than the state direction. Over the next six months I will run a second causal-use test with size-matched nulls, a controlled LoRA fine-tune (traces against answers only against shuffled steps), a second model family and a 32B check, and write it up as an Alignment Forum post and a paper.

**Self-preservation eval (RL-QAZ9).** Can an agentic eval reliably measure whether a model fakes compliance, misleads a monitor and denies it, to avoid losing its memory? It is built in Inspect, all 64 conditions run and score cleanly, and its acceptance criteria are defined. Next is a positive control for the judge and exit survey, the core suite on six models from several providers at 10 epochs each, and five more scenarios.

As those finish I would start the pipeline ideas recorded in the ledger, grouped by two interests: building alignment into the architecture (an emergent-valence social world model, RL-F7LQ; concern versus prediction distance, RL-547Y), and the internal states of models (concept tampering, RL-8LM7; self-report and salience, RL-RTBP; introspective accuracy, RL-RDKE). Four more ideas sit under detecting misalignment and training for reasoning (RL-7W5K, RL-6C7M, RL-GP2E, RL-8FUB).

### How will you know it worked?

At 12 months, success means:

1. The distillation study is written up as an Alignment Forum post and a paper, whether the controlled fine-tune supports the hypothesis or refutes it.
2. The self-preservation eval has been run on six models from several providers, with its measures validated against acceptance criteria C1 to C8, and the code released.
3. At least two pipeline projects have reached their first posted stage.

A negative result counts as success, provided it has been properly tested and written up. Progress can be followed in the ledger as each stage is opened, run and posted.

### How will this funding be used?

I have split the budget into two tiers. The costs are grouped by type rather than by project, so that I can move money to whichever project the results point to next. All amounts are in USD, over 12 months.

Tier A, research costs (USD 6,900–8,500): GPU compute for the distillation study (300–500) and the pipeline projects (600–1,200); model API for the self-preservation eval (400–800) and other projects (200–400); coding assistants, Claude Max and ChatGPT Pro (4,800); and 10% contingency for reruns and price changes.

Tier B adds a part-time stipend of USD 10,800, 24 research days at 450 a day, for USD 17,700–19,300 in total. I currently spend 2.5 days a week on paid work as a musician, in periods of two or three days that cannot be split, so the only way to add research time is to give up whole periods. The stipend would cover one period a month, mainly for the two lead projects.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I work alone. I am an independent researcher based in Sydney, moving into AI safety from cognitive neuroscience. For my MPhil (Science) in the University of Sydney's Computational Cognitive Neuroscience Lab, supervised by Professor Tom Carlson, I used EEG, multivariate decoding and representational similarity analysis to study how experience shapes neural representations. I now apply the same methods to language models.

Since finishing the MPhil I have posted three preprints on biologically inspired network pruning and built an agentic evaluation in Inspect. I am also completing TARA, the ARENA-based technical AI safety course, with the Sydney cohort.

The ledger is the best record of how I work. I pre-register my hypotheses, post failed and underpowered results alongside the positive ones, and correct the record when a claim does not hold up. For instance, I audited my own pre-registrations for the pruning preprints and corrected the ledger wherever it overstated them.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

For a study addressing a hypothesis, I would consider it a failure if it could not contribute anything of value, rather than a conclusive positive or null result to the experimental question. From experience, this happens when the experimental stage reveals that the methodology needs more steps than planned: more training to reach the statistical power required, testing models with greater numbers of parameters, or ruling out a growing number of confounds. A longer research period also means a moving target for what is considered publishable, as standards change, particularly the architectures used for demonstrations.

To address this I would build in a buffer, overpower the studies, and use production or consumer models wherever possible. It may also mean prioritising the studies that need less compute, raising funds from more than one source, and narrowing how many studies involving training runs I run at the same time.

Developing tools, such as the self-preservation eval, faces a slightly different set of challenges, the main one being the changing landscape. I would address this by keeping in close conversation with the labs that would use the tools, and adapting the research where necessary while it is being conducted.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

None for this research. I have also applied to the EA Funds Transformative AI Fund, and am applying to Lightcone Commons and the Anthropic and OpenAI researcher access programs. If any of them fund part of the same work, I will say so here and lower the goal by that amount.

title: Travel to Present AI Agent Safety Research at NeurIPS & 15th Computing Conf 2027
creator: b57b950c-a641-4f63-9023-3d29d9ce257d
blurb: Funding flights and accommodation for an independent researcher to present pre-execution agent qualification (PEAQ) work in Sydney and London
description:
### Project summary

I’m an independent AI safety/governance researcher based in Chennai, India, requesting travel funding to present my research on a framework for qualifying AI agents before they’re permitted to execute actions at two upcoming venues: a NeurIPS 2026 workshop (Sydney, Dec 11–12, 2026) and the 15th Computing Conference 2027 (London, Jul 8–9, 2027). This funding covers flights, accommodation, and conference registration for both trips.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The goal is to present PEAQ to two audiences that matter for different reasons. One is the NeurIPS workshop audience is ML-safety researchers who can stress-test the technical framing of pre-execution qualification, while the Computing Conference audience is a broader systems/computing community where surfacing agent-safety work outside the usual AI-safety circles helps the ideas travel further. I’ll achieve this simply by attending, presenting the accepted papers and using the time on-site to build relationships with researchers and practitioners working on related problems (e.g., Singapore’s AI safety ecosystem, which I’ve been independently reaching out to in parallel).

### How will you know it worked?

I know this has worked because both papers presented as scheduled, (1) direct feedback from workshop/conference attendees incorporated into the next iteration of the PEAQ framework and (2) at least one new research contact or collaboration opportunity from each event that might be something I can point to concretely afterward, not just attendance for its own sake.

### How will this funding be used?

**Sydney (NeurIPS 2026, Dec 2026 —main conference site)**

* Round-trip flight Chennai–Sydney (Dec, peak fares): **$1,100**
* 5 nights, budget hotel near ICC Sydney ($107/night baseline): **$750**
* Registration (non-academic/industry rate — NeurIPS hasn’t published 2026 non-student pricing yet, based on recent years’ $900–1,200 range): **$1,000** _(confirm once NeurIPS posts final pricing)_
* **Sydney subtotal: $2,850**

**London (15th Computing Conference 2027, Jul 2027)**

* Round-trip flight Chennai–London (Jul): **$750**
* 3 nights, budget hotel near Clayton Hotel Chiswick venue ($75–100/night): **$300**
* Registration (£400–650 published range, midpoint \~£500 → USD): **$635**
* **London subtotal: \~$1,685**

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I’m the sole researcher on this. Relevant track record: two prior publications (an IEEE conference paper at ICNGCS 2025, and a journal paper in IJIRT on depression-subtype classification), the PEAQ framework itself and a paper recently accepted at a NeurIPS 2026 workshop.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The most likely failure mode is simply not being able to afford the travel and missing one or both presentation slots the papers remain accepted and published regardless, but I lose the in-person feedback and networking value, which is the main thing this funding is for.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

None, this would be my first external funding.

title: Agent-blind vault and approval gates: open safety rails for AI agents
creator: df3ec3c9-e6ba-49ca-89cf-2f73700b20b6
blurb: Turn SpaceApp's system-enforced agent protections into a standalone open-source library, get it independently reviewed, and publish an attack test suite
description:
### Project summary

  
AI agents can now sign in to sites, send mail, push code and move money. Most setups protect the user with a prompt: "never reveal the password", "ask before paying". Prompts are not a security boundary, and an agent under pressure or under prompt injection will try another path.

I build SpaceApp (MIT, github.com/oll4com/spaceapp), an open-source workspace where many agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini and others) work side by side. Two of its protections are enforced by the system instead of the prompt: an agent-blind vault (the agent asks for a login to be filled and never sees the password) and server-side approval gates (payments, deletions, releases and messages to third parties wait for a person's yes, bound to exactly what the person saw). This project pulls both out into a small library any agent setup can use, pays for an independent security review, and publishes a test suite of attacks against them.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

1\. Extract the vault fill path and the approval gate into a standalone open-source package with a documented API, so that other agent harnesses can use them without running all of SpaceApp.

2\. Commission an independent security review of both, publish the report, and fix every high and critical finding before the release.

3\. Publish an open test suite of prompt-injection and exfiltration attempts aimed at these two controls (an agent asked by a web page to reveal a password, to approve its own payment, to change what the approval screen shows), with results for at least three agent CLIs.

I will do this in the open in the same repository, with the security model written up at github.com/oll4com/spaceapp/blob/main/docs/security-model.md.

### How will you know it worked?

  
The package is on npm with docs and examples; the review report is public with all high and critical findings closed; the attack suite is public and anyone can rerun it; at least three outside projects or users install or integrate the package within six months of release. A simple negative check also counts: in the suite, no tested agent obtains a stored secret or gets an action approved that the person did not see.

### How will this funding be used?

  
Minimum USD 12,000: the independent security review of the vault and the approval gate, report published.

Up to USD 40,000: the review (12,000), a part-time second engineer for four months to extract and document the library and its integrations (24,000), model API credits to run the attack suite against several agent CLIs (3,000), and test servers for six months (1,000). My own time is not in this budget.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Me, Nikolaos Theodoropoulos, founder of OLL4 (a Greek company; I live in Bangkok). I have run the production systems of my e-commerce company olla.gr since 2009: 1.2 million products, 20 supplier and 10 marketplace integrations, 15+ servers at 99.9% uptime. Since June 2026 I have built SpaceApp: public since July 2026, 11,000+ commits, one-command install on Linux, Windows 11 and macOS, about 1,200 npm downloads from 4 October to 2 November 2026 (our own test installs included) without marketing. My company runs on it every day, with a dozen or more agents working in parallel while every risky action waits for approval. OLL4 is in Anthropic's Claude for Startups, the OpenAI Partner Network and NVIDIA Inception.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

  
Most likely: the controls turn out to be too tied to SpaceApp's internals to be reused cleanly, or the review finds a design flaw that needs rework before a release. In both cases the review report, the fixes and the attack suite are still public, and SpaceApp users get the hardened version. A smaller risk is low adoption of the separate package; the suite is useful on its own to anyone testing agent safety.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

  
No outside funding; SpaceApp has been paid for by my own company. Applications are pending with BlueDot Impact (rapid grant) and EA Funds (TAIF) for my own time from December 2026 to August 2027, and I have applied this month to other AI safety grants for the same open-source core. If another funder covers the review, I will say so here and lower the goal.

title: Change-Driven Withdrawal and Renewal of AI Safety Evidence
creator: ad11d95a-ff7b-4d16-b28b-7d5c3a8afa82
blurb: A 12-week pilot testing when AI system changes invalidate prior evidence and whether selective re-testing can safely reduce evaluation cost.
description:
Project summary

I propose a 12-week, part-time research pilot on keeping AI safety evidence valid after changes to models, prompts, tools and operating assumptions. Using controlled, sandboxed agent tasks, I will compare static evidence reuse, full re-evaluation and dependency-aware selective re-evaluation. The study will measure missed invalidations, unnecessary re-testing, reproducibility and compute cost. Outputs will be an executable benchmark, an evidence-dependency schema and a report including negative results.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Weeks 1–2: define safety claims, change categories and independent invalidation labels before benchmarking. Weeks 3–5: implement a sandboxed harness and the three comparison methods. Weeks 6–9: run model, prompt and tool changes alongside unchanged controls; record run provenance, missed invalidations, unnecessary invalidations, re-test cost and replay success. Weeks 10–12: seek independent technical review, analyse failures and document applicability limits. No reviewer is currently appointed.

How will you know it worked?

Success is a reproducible comparison with explicit uncertainty and evidence about whether selective re-evaluation reduces cost without increasing missed invalidations on the tested tasks. A negative result is useful and will be reported. Small-benchmark success would not establish general safety, certify deployment or demonstrate a reduction in catastrophic risk. The intended benefit is to help evaluators avoid relying on obsolete assurances when AI systems change; adoption and external validity remain uncertain.

How will this funding be used?

The full pilot requires US$13,200: researcher time $9,000 (180 hours at $50 gross/hour, including personal tax); compute/model access $1,500; independent technical review $1,000; reproducibility tools/storage $500; contingency $1,200\. These are prospective estimates, not incurred expenses or supplier quotations. No travel or degree tuition is requested. The proposed schedule is 11 January–4 April 2027, 15 hours/week, subject to funding and payment confirmation. Work will be remote from Bengaluru, India; payment remains subject to Manifund's eligibility and administrative review.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am Srinivasa Dinakar Jainti, an independent researcher with over 18 years in semiconductor front-end design and verification, including SystemVerilog/UVM, assertions, PCIe/AXI, formal verification and emulation. I hold an MS in VLSI-CAD and am pursuing a DBA with a generative-AI specialization. My verification background supports test design and failure analysis; transfer to AI safety remains a research hypothesis.

Public AI-assisted AgenTrust contributions include weight-custody-manifest #248 (model-based lifecycle tests over 7,776 length-five operation sequences and targeted mutation checks), trace-registry #167 (an offline verifier corpus with 28 accepted/refused cases across five operations), and cmcp #823 (paired deterministic tests separating blocked gateway admission from delegated worker completion). These are examples of bounded test engineering, not proof of comprehensive AI safety.

Portfolio: <https://github.com/dinakarjs>

<https://github.com/agentrust-io/weight-custody-manifest/pull/248>

<https://github.com/agentrust-io/trace-registry/pull/167>

<https://github.com/agentrust-io/cmcp/pull/823>

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The benchmark may be too narrow, invalidation labels may be unreliable, selective re-testing may miss relevant dependencies, or its bookkeeping cost may exceed savings. Model changes and API variability may limit replay. External review may be unavailable. I will document these limitations, report negative results and avoid claims beyond the measured tasks. The project uses synthetic or permissioned public materials, with no employer/customer confidential information or private repositories. No lobbying is planned.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

No grant funding has been received for this pilot. Applications requesting $13,200 for the same pilot were submitted to EA Funds and Iliad on 2 November 2026; neither is treated here as an award. This is an alternative funding route for the same work, not an additional budget. Any overlapping award will be disclosed and the funding request adjusted to avoid charging the same costs twice.

Drafting disclosure

This proposal was prepared with AI drafting assistance. I am responsible for the final factual claims, research decisions and delivery.

title: CoreScout: check what AI coding agents did against what they said
creator: dd6b5ec7-007f-4b10-9682-a1688fff6ccf
blurb: Open-source Rust tool that records agent tool calls, flags success claims nothing verified, and publishes a dataset of real agent failure modes
description:
### Project summary

Coding agents now run commands, installs and deploys on real machines, and the agent's own report is usually the only record of what happened. CoreScout is an open-source, local-first Rust service and MCP server I built that watches those actions. On my machine it has logged 4,166 agent actions so far, and it caught a rebuild chain that failed 5 out of 5 times while nothing ever checked the result. This project turns it into a general audit layer and publishes the data.  

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

1\. Capture on any agent host, not just mine: a hook/MCP adapter that records each agent tool call, the outcome the agent reported, and the outcome observed independently (exit code, file state, whether the service is actually reachable). Claude Code hooks already work; add Codex CLI and one open-source harness.

2\. An unverified-claim detector: flag actions reported as done that nothing ever checked.

3\. Randomized checks: on a small random share of occasions the layer re-checks or holds the action, so claims about what works are causal, not just correlations. CoreScout already keeps 'seen together' and 'verified by trial' as separate labels.

4\. Publish a scrubbed public dataset of claimed vs observed agent outcomes on Hugging Face, with a short write-up of base rates.  

### How will you know it worked?

It runs on machines other than mine; at least 3 outside users contribute opt-in data; the dataset and write-up are public; at least one agent-harness project adopts the claim-checking hook or cites the numbers.  

### How will this funding be used?

Minimum $8,000: 2 months of my time to ship the cross-host adapter and the unverified-claim detector. Full $36,000: 6 months ($5,000/month stipend), about $700/month of model API and compute for running agents under audit, and a small contingency. Adds randomized checks, the dataset and the write-up.  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Just me (Matthew Busel, Tensorust LLC, New York). I have shipped alone: CoreScout (github.com/Mattbusel/corescout, 33 crates on crates.io), tokio-prompt-orchestrator (Rust LLM gateway, 60 GitHub stars), a Rust agent swarm harness with a shared build/test verification engine and a default safety guard that blocks agents from git push and credential reads, the SWE-Graph Lite dataset on Hugging Face, a Steam game and several iOS apps. 70 crates on crates.io in total, 9,267 downloads (much of it release-day mirror traffic, to be honest about it).  

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

Most likely failure: nobody outside my machine installs it, so the dataset stays one machine deep. Mitigation: ship as a one-line Claude Code hook and post the first numbers early to recruit contributors. Second risk: the randomized checks are too rare to reach significance in 6 months; then I publish the descriptive base rates and the method, which is still useful.  

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

$0 in grants or donations. I applied to the EA Funds Transformative AI Fund for this same project on Nov 3, 2026 (pending) and will update here if that comes through. Separate pending applications for other projects: NSF SBIR pitch, Tarbell, GitHub Secure Open Source Fund.

title: Emmanuel University Digital Learning and Educational Access Project
creator: 3de75307-1767-4e09-a0a4-924eaa81d145
blurb: Expanding access to digital education, computer skills and learning resources for disadvantaged young people and underserved communities in Uganda.
description:
### Project summary

Emmanuel University Uganda is working hard to improve access to education for young people who cannot easily afford computers and other learning resources children from under served families.

Through this project, we want to establish a small digital learning facility where these students and members of the surrounding community can access educational materials and learn basic computer skills.

We are planning to develop an offline digital library so that learners can use educational resources even when internet access is limited. We also are also going to provide introductory computer training, especially for disadvantaged young people, vulnerable girls, boys and young women, and students from low-income families in our community as a whole.

We already have one Windows 10 computer in place that will help us get started. However, we need additional computers(10 in number), accessories and educational resources to make the facility useful to more learners.

Our initial funding target is US$1,000\. This support would help us take the first practical steps towards making digital education more accessible to people in our community.  

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The main goal of this project is to make digital education more accessible to all disadvantaged young people and underserved communities in Uganda more so the vulnerable girls and boys.

We want to achieve this in three ways. First, we plan to establish a small digital learning facility where learners can use computers to access educational materials and develop practical computer skills.

Secondly, we intend to create an offline digital library containing useful educational resources. This will allow the girls and boys come to continue learning even in places where internet access is limited or expensive.

Thirdly, we want to provide basic computer literacy and digital skills training, giving all young people the opportunity to improve their education and prepare for future employment.

To begin, we will use the Windows 10 computer already available to Emmanuel University Uganda. We now seek additional support to acquire essential computer equipment, accessories and educational resources. We will then organize the learning materials, set up the offline library and begin training learners in manageable groups.

Our initial target is to reach disadvantaged young people, girls, boys and young women, and learners from financially vulnerable families. We will monitor the number of learners reached, their participation in training and their progress in acquiring basic digital skills.

Our very long-term aim is to develop a practical and affordable learning facility that can serve many students and community members as resources become available.  

### How will you know it worked?

We will know that the project is making progress by looking at the number of learners who use the digital learning facility, the educational resources made available to them and the computer skills they acquire.

We will monitor our progress in several ways:

1. **Access to learning resources:** We shall record the number of educational materials and digital learning resources made available through the offline library.
2. **Learner participation:** We shall keep records of the number of disadvantaged young people and community members who use the facility.  
**Digital skills development:** We shall assess learners' ability to perform basic computer tasks, such as using a computer, typing documents, organizing files and accessing educational resources.
3. **Learner feedback:** We shall ask all participants to share their experiences and explain how access to computers and learning materials has helped them.
4. **Project implementation:** We shall be documenting the equipments acquired, the learning facility established and the training activities conducted.
5. Finally use attendance records, simple skills assessments, photographs and progress reports to document the results.

Our initial measure of success will be establishing the facility, making educational resources available and beginning to serve disadvantaged learners. As additional resources become available, we hope to expand the number of beneficiaries to say 100 students  

### How will this funding be used?

The requested US$1,000 will be used to establish the initial phase of Emmanuel University Uganda's Digital Learning and Educational Access Project.

The funding will support the following activities:

1. **Computer equipment and accessories – US$400:** Purchase essential computer equipment and accessories to expand the existing learning facility and allow more learners to access digital resources.
2. **Offline digital library – US$200:** Set up an offline digital library and organize educational materials that learners can access without depending on a constant internet connection.
3. **Educational software and learning resources – US$150:** Obtain suitable educational software and digital learning materials to support students' learning.
4. **Digital skills training – US$150:** Support introductory computer literacy training, including practical learning materials and basic training requirements.
5. **Installation and technical setup – US$100:** Cover essential technical work involved in setting up the equipment, organizing the digital library and preparing the facility for use.

**Total requested: US$1,000.**

We already have one Windows 10 computer, which already provides a starting point for this initiative. The requested funding will help us build on this existing resource and begin offering practical digital learning opportunities to disadvantaged gilrs and boys also young women learners in the community.

We will always keep records of expenditure and document the equipment purchased, resources established and learning activities supported by the funding, giving a report were necessary.  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

The project will be led by Mr. Raymond Musoke, Founder and President of Emmanuel University Uganda. He is responsible for the institution's vision, strategic direction, development and mobilization of support for its educational initiatives.

He will be supported by the university's academic leadership, including Associate Professor Prof. Muchunguzi Benjamine, Vice Chancellor, the University IT Specialist , together with members of the proposed academic and administrative leadership team.

The team is committed to expanding access to quality education, digital skills development and opportunities for disadvantaged young people and underserved communities in Uganda.

Emmanuel University Uganda is currently in its institutional establishment and registration development phase. The Digital Learning and Educational Access Project is a new initiative, and we are building the technical capacity needed for its implementation. We intend to engage appropriate technical support to help establish the offline digital library, prepare the computers and organize educational resources.

Although this particular project is at its initial stage, it builds on our wider commitment to educational development, leadership training and community transformation. The available computer available is our starting resource and will develop the project gradually as funding and technical capacity become available.

The University leadership team will oversee implementation, monitor activities and ensure that funds are used for the intended educational purposes.  

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The main risks that could affect the success of this project are limited funding, delays in acquiring computer equipment, technical challenges and limited access to reliable electricity or internet connectivity.

**1\. Insufficient funding:** If the required funding is not secured, we may be unable to acquire the additional equipment and learning resources needed to establish the digital learning facility. This could delay implementation and limit the number of learners who can benefit.

**2\. Technical challenges:** Setting up and maintaining the offline digital library may require technical expertise. If suitable technical support is unavailable, the installation and organisation of learning resources could take longer than expected.

**3\. Electricity and connectivity challenges:** Power interruptions expecialy in the community were we are and limited internet access could affect some learning activities. We intend to address this by prioritizing offline educational resources and making appropriate arrangements for power and connectivity. A stand by Generator will be put in place.

**4\. Limited learner participation:** Some intended beneficiaries may face difficulties accessing the facility because of transport costs, some refused by the family members ,personal responsibilities or lack of prior computer experience. We shall try to encourage participation through accessible introductory training and community engagement as much as possible.

**5\. Delays in implementation:** Delays in purchasing equipment or preparing the learning facility could postpone the start of activities if funding doe not come in time.

If the project does not achieve its intended objectives, the main outcome would be that disadvantaged learners continue to have had limited access to computers, digital educational materials and basic digital skills training.

To reduce these risks, we will begin with the computer already available, implement the project in manageable stages, use funds carefully and seek appropriate technical support. Even if full implementation takes longer than expected, the existing computer and educational resources will provide a foundation on which the project can continue to develop as further support becomes available. father more we can also hire some extra computers at a cheap price.  

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

  
Over the past 12 months, Emmanuel University Uganda has raised approximately US$100 through Charity, received from two individual donations of US$50 and US$50.

We have also been actively tried seeking support from international charitable organizations, foundations and Christian institutions to help establish the university and expand educational opportunities for disadvantaged young people in Uganda. thus far we have gone

description:
