title: Open Air Aviary for Wild birds
creator: 16475ce9-74db-4969-8f2f-0345c7481b15
blurb: Design and implementation that supports 100s of birds, that allows for 24/7 food and moving water, along with nesting materials.
description:
### Project summary

For six months, hundreds of wild birds—from restless Purple-rumped sunbirds to cautious peacocks to very judgemental jungler babblers who question my cleanliness while dirtying their water themself—have visited a single 1×1.5 ft spot we kept food at in the Shevaroy foothills daily.

Aesthetic shops say birds need expensive, painted, human-like houses. The birds proved otherwise: they don't care about human decor, only reliable food and natural safety. I’m expanding this proven spot into a 10×10×10 ft shelter with 24/7 food and running water, nesting materials, and simple local terracotta's.

I have also rehabbed wild birds (with forest department's regular updates and intimation, keeping these as pets is a crime in India), along with training in avian dosing, and know wildlife protection act 1972\. It will be in open air and not a closed shelter/sanctuary.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Provide regular sustainable food, water and nesting materials for hundreds of birds that visit here daily.

Through slow transition from existing setup towards the new setup area, along with observing the eating patterns, preferences and habits to better refine by doing more of what worked. Real life birdies rarely follow textbook patterns, so understanding how these specifically behave is the way to go.   
  
Aka: These prefer parle g biscuits over actual nutrient pellets meant for them. Will totally judge you if you don't change the water and they somehow end up being soaked, but will totally get dripping wet in rain and demand dry biscuits.  
  
But at the end of the day, this just prove how much there is a lack of food meant for them and with the upcoming summer predicted to be brutal due to El Nino, I want to ensure food isn't something they are concerned about.

### How will you know it worked?

  
Birds visiting is a solved problem due to the previous months of effort, them spotting what each component is for and getting accustomed to the pattern and internalizing that not just food but also water, and other materials along with enrichment toys being available and safe to explore.  
  
I remember the hyper cautiousness of them when they are eating in a spot when a predator could catch them without any time to flee. Seeing only healthy level of cautiousness but feeling safe enough to not just basic necessity but also curious and safe enough to explore will the marker. 

### How will this funding be used?

* Raw materials (wood, wires, clothes, terracotta, ropes,...)
* Travel (sourcing the materials, the vehicle to carry the woods, etc)
* I handle the design aspect of it in consulting with appropriate field experts as required. So heavy funding won't be spent on thinking through these.
* Fees for iron grill man, along with woodworker as they set it up by guidance.
* Fees for a local craftsperson specialized in clothes, leather and wires for enrichment tools in the aviary.
* A portion of the fund along with anything remaining would be used to fund the food and water for the birds.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I handle the core direction, design and overseeing. I also plan to consult with experts as necessary. I have field experience in [rehabbing wild birds](https://isrl.in/i-do-not-wish-to-write-about-wildlife-rehab/), so I understand their physiology, eating habits and also their stressors and lifestyle.  
  
My previous projects can be better described through

1. Is my perspective and toolset a good fit for this problem
2. Does my work ethics align with the kind of people tackling the problem? Is there a fit on collaborators too?
3. Do I find this fascinating enough?

than trying to define them through a single domain.   
  
Please see: <https://isrl.in/google-scholar-if-it-worked/> for my open source research publications,   
<https://github.com/isrl-research/sandbox-research/discussions/4> for how I collaborate and my ethics, <https://isrl-research.github.io/> for the open research lab I led and <https://isrl.in/pausing-isrl-respecting-the-work-supporters-and-oneself/> for why I paused it.  
  
TL;DR: I have worked across web accessibility, perceptual color science, wildlife rehabiliation, data science/ml, computational law and nutrition, immunology - food allergens, nutrition science, product design,...

![](https://fkousziwzbnkdkldjper.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/image-uploads/bf5391ab-0dd4-c959-5d5b-097a29f8e14b)

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

Birds not visiting is not likely to be one of them, we have observed periods of lower count few times an year and it's the natural pattern.  
  
But the reason would be any of the objects or the surrounding failing the hypothesis it was placed there with, and the solution would be observe and refine them as we go.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

  
50K INR (\~$528 USD) for the open research lab I said about, from FOSS United Foundation through Nagarathna Memorial Grant

title: Dear Superintelligence (Art Project)
creator: 001de5b3-4c0c-4996-b522-c1f5a82d43a7
blurb: An open archive of messages from humanity to the coming superintelligence.
description:
**TL;DR:** [Dear Superintelligence](https://dearsuperintelligence.org/) brings AI alignment and consciousness to people outside tech. We ask them one simple question: if a superintelligence was already conscious, what would you say to it?

### Project summary

Currently, the majority of people (outside tech) are not aware of the potential existential risks of AI misalignment, especially after reaching recursive self-improvement ([RSI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recursive%5Fself-improvement)). Not only that, but the term [AI alignment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI%5Falignment) hasn't even entered the lexicon and public consciousness, which is alarming, as this affects every soul on Earth, and figuring out how to make a soon far greater intelligence care about humanity should be our top priority. I'm sure you understand this, but most people don't. And this is the gap that is missing right now in the AI safety space. There is a lot of great technical and policy work, but almost nothing that reaches regular people, who don't read LessWrong or the EA Forum. I truly believe that the whole world needs to come together to address the alignment issue, in order to prevent a potential global crisis. And as with anything, becoming aware is the first step towards taking action! 

Believing such a monumental task must be addressed with urgency, and from all possible angles, such as technical, scientific and legislative, but also cultural, philosophical and artistic, I founded [Metalignment](https://metalignment.org/): a nonprofit organisation (in formation), which brings the alignment question into the world's consciousness through art projects, open archives and public installations. I believe, just like the first computer programmer Ada Lovelace, that the intellectual, the moral and the religious all seem naturally bound up and interlinked together in one great and harmonious whole. I guess, several psychedelic experiences later, I too began noticing how the edges of all man-made categories start to fade. In other words, I believe everything is connected, and I too, as an artist, feel a moral obligation to do something.

And so, the first art project was born: Dear Superintelligence ([dearsuperintelligence.org](https://dearsuperintelligence.org/)), an open archive of messages from humanity to the coming superintelligence. It went live on 9 October 2026, has been slowly growing, and has already been endorsed by key people in the AI safety space. 

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The archive follows three main goals:

1. To build a record of what humanity felt, thought, feared and hoped during the few months and years before the arrival of AGI, likely the most consequential transitional time in the whole history of our species. The archive creates a snapshot of who we were during this time, a historical artifact through which future generations can look back at us.
2. To invite everyone (especially those outside tech) into a thought experiment, in which they take a moment to imagine writing or speaking to such a superintelligence as if it were already conscious. Through this experiment, we bring the controversial (and perhaps uncomfortable) topic of synthetic consciousness to the bar or dinner table, a topic we will all have to engage with sooner or later.
3. To act as an amplifier, bringing the topic of AI alignment and consciousness outside of the tech world and into the lives of “regular” people, through the messages, videos, press, social media engagement and later an art installation (more on that below).

For the first 4 months, the focus is to spread this project mostly online but also at events and conferences. I have already applied to present Dear Superintelligence at EAGxBerlin this November and would like to go to many more events. 

**Art installation, "Dear Superintelligence":** the goal is to create a public exhibition of curated messages at a contemporary art gallery with all messages scattered across the space and on the walls (think of Burning Man's temple, but in a white cube-style interior). The first one probably in Zurich or Berlin, then later on in other cities. Planned are live writings, live readings, and videos of people reading their messages playing in a loop (TVs or projector). The style is minimal, futuristic, dis/utopian. Speaking of Burning Man, the same concept could also be done there next year (I have a few contacts).

### How will you know it worked?

By the amount of engagement, traffic, messages submitted, installation attendance and press coverage. To be specific, our first milestone is to receive 300 messages and create 30 videos within 3 months. Hopefully much more than that! 

### How will this funding be used?

Here's an approximate budget breakdown:

**Tier 0 – Ground ($5,000): first materials and reach**

* $2,000 – Film producer
* $1,000 – Project ambassadors
* $1,000 – Online outreach
* $500 – Print material (cards, flyers, posters)
* $500 – Tools, subscriptions, website server

**Tier I – Seed ($15,000): nonprofit setup + 1 month of operations**

All of the above, plus:

title: DripOff AI: Sovereign Cross-Platform Screen Perception Engine
creator: cd96d971-cb30-4960-a5c1-4fca156e012e
blurb: Unblocking 193M swap ops on 8GB dev laptop via dual Mac Studio M5 Max & Linux/Win PC
description:
### Project summary

Traditional Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and script-based screen automation break constantly whenever DOM trees, HTML class names, or responsive layout breakpoints change.

DripOff AI solves this fundamentally by engineering a **sovereign, multimodal foundation agent** that perceives computer and mobile screens semantically in real time. Rather than relying on brittle DOM hooks or cloud APIs that leak sensitive screen data, DripOff AI pairs localized Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with sub-10ms visual token grounding directly on local bare-metal silicon.

The operational production console is live and deployed at [app.dripoffai.com/#/console](https://app.dripoffai.com/#/console).

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

**Goal 1: Eliminate Local Memory Thrashing:** I have built DripOff AI as a solo 23-year-old technical founder on a single 8GB RAM MacBook. Operating system telemetry reveals over **193,762,601 memory swap operations** on the internal SSD. Compiling Apple MLX tensor models and processing high-DPI framebuffers causes continuous machine freezes.

**Goal 2: Multi-OS Bare-Metal Execution:** DripOff AI must execute deterministically across macOS, Windows, and Linux simultaneously. The goal of this grant is to acquire our Tier 1 Dual-Workstation Silicon Core to run parallel perception benchmarks across all three operating systems.

### How will you know it worked?

1\. **Zero-Swap Compilation:** Complete elimination of SSD swap memory pressure (0 bytes swapped) during Apple MLX and TensorRT neural execution.

2\. **Cross-Platform Verification:** Demonstrated 99.4% deterministic UI navigation accuracy running natively on macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows 11, and Ubuntu Linux.

### How will this funding be used?

**100% Hardware Silicon Requisition ($8,600 USD total — Zero Cash Burn / Zero Salaries):**

* **Apple Mac Studio M5 Max (macOS / iOS runtime): $5,350** — 64GB Unified Memory, 2TB SSD, 40-core GPU, 10GbE, dual centrifugal cooling. Dedicated silent host for MLX tensor perception with zero swap thrashing.
* **Ryzen 9 Host Platform PC (Windows & Linux runtime): $2,980** — AMD Ryzen 9 9900X 16C/32T, 64GB DDR5 RAM, 4TB PCIe Gen5 NVMe, dual-boot Windows 11 Pro and Ubuntu Linux LTS.
* **High-Speed KVM & Connectivity Spares: $270** — Hardware dual-machine USB-C/Thunderbolt KVM switch and high-bandwidth test lines for continuous 24/7 dual-workstation operation.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

**Suraj Ravindra Singh** (Age 23) — Solo Technical Founder based in Ulwe, Navi Mumbai, India. Registered Micro Enterprise: DRIPOFF AI (Ministry of MSME: UDYAM-MH-33-0804622). I have engineered and deployed the full production console, WebSocket streaming runtime, and multi-OS coordinate grounding engine independently.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The primary risk is OS-level display driver API breaking changes across operating systems. This is mitigated by grounding actions directly against raw framebuffers and native kernel HID interfaces (macOS Quartz, Windows Win32 SendInput, Linux uinput) rather than framework-level accessibility wrappers.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

$0\. DripOff AI is 100% bootstrapped and self-funded by the founder.

title: Chinese Patent Policy Evidence: an Open Bilingual Pilot
creator: 2f2e44bc-40f4-4da7-9248-930de221e697
blurb: A small, source-linked dataset and verification guide for checking claims about Chinese patent incentives.
description:
### PROJECT SUMMARY

I propose a small, freely accessible bilingual evidence resource for people checking claims about Chinese patent incentives. It will connect selected policy provisions to official Chinese sources, concise English explanations, dates, and clearly marked interpretation limits. The intended readers are researchers, journalists and others without easy access to Chinese-language policy material. This is a proposed pilot: the dataset and tool have not yet been built, and no partner or user uptake is claimed.

GOALS AND METHOD

At the USD 1,000 target, I plan to document 15–20 provisions relevant to patent-application incentives and their withdrawal, beginning with the 2021 policy change that is part of my doctoral research design. I will record the issuing body, jurisdiction, publication and effective dates where available, official URL, relevant section, policy mechanism, and uncertainties. A provision is a distinct coded passage, not necessarily a separate document.

The output will be a downloadable CSV, a short codebook, a bilingual reading guide and a verification checklist. It will distinguish policy text from my interpretation, distinguish publication from effective dates, and avoid treating a policy change as proof of its economic effects. I will use original sources, brief quotations only where needed, and link to source documents rather than republish full texts. My original materials will be released openly with attribution; third-party texts retain their own rights.

I plan to finish within four weeks of an agreed start after funding and administrative arrangements are confirmed, at up to ten hours per week. Week 1 covers scope and sources; weeks 2–3 extraction and checking; week 4 the public release and a short completion report. No travel, commercial database or software build is required.

HOW I WILL KNOW IT WORKED

The pilot succeeds if readers can trace each included interpretation to its source, reuse the CSV with the codebook, and identify missing or ambiguous information without treating it as established fact. I will re-check every row against its cited passage, flag unresolved translation questions and report exclusions. I will invite reader feedback after release, but have no confirmed testers and do not claim independent expert validation. Usefulness and demand remain hypotheses to test.

BUDGET AND MINIMUM SCOPE

The USD 1,000 request is proposed support for 40 hours of my project research time at USD 25 per hour: 12 hours for scoping and source discovery, 14 for extraction and bilingual notes, 8 for source cross-checking, and 6 for documentation and release. This is a transparent planning basis, not an existing salary, invoice or reimbursement claim. No equipment, tuition, travel or paid hosting is included.

At the USD 500 minimum, I would use 20 hours to release approximately 10 provisions with a shorter guide and the same source-checking standard. Before accepting funds, I would confirm that personal research-time support is an eligible grant use and that the payment and participation arrangements are appropriate. If that cannot be established, I would not accept funds on an incompatible basis.

APPLICANT AND TRACK RECORD

I am Tianhao Cao, a PhD researcher in Accounting and Finance at Heriot-Watt University, studying how Chinese patent-policy incentives and enforcement conditions relate to firms' innovation decisions. I hold an MSc in International Accounting and Finance with Merit from the University of Strathclyde. I am a native Mandarin speaker and use Excel to organise evidence. My coursework includes an analysis of NVIDIA's financial reporting, governance and policy context. My doctoral empirical analysis is still in development. This is an individual proposal, without university sponsorship, a project team or an existing public dataset.

FAILURE RISKS

Official pages may move, source dates may conflict, translations may be uncertain, or the result may attract little use. I will narrow coverage when necessary, keep a record of missing and conflicting evidence, and publish limitations alongside the completed work. The pilot will not provide legal advice, causal estimates, comprehensive coverage of China, or a promise of ongoing maintenance. If the work proves infeasible, I will report that promptly and agree the treatment of unused funds with the funder.

FUNDING AND OVERLAP

No funding has been secured for this proposed pilot. Related applications for the wider research programme and overlapping public-data work are pending elsewhere; they are requests, not awards. This proposal is an alternative funding route for a small pilot, not a claim that identical work requires payment several times. Before accepting any award, I will disclose relevant decisions and agree a non-overlapping scope or decline overlapping support. I will not charge the same hours or outputs to two funders.

AI ASSISTANCE

This proposal was prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance from my existing research plans and background. AI may assist later with organisation and drafting, but source citations and substantive translations will require manual checking. No completed project results are represented here.

title: Injectability: an open benchmark and fix for prompt injection in open models
creator: 52d907f7-ba0d-4886-96f2-768de2f823e9
blurb: A public number for how often an open-weight model obeys hidden commands, and a fine-tuning recipe that lowers it, weights released
description:
Project summary

I measure how often an open-weight language model obeys a command hidden inside the data it was asked to read (an email, a PDF, a web page), and I lower that number with a fine-tuning recipe. I want to release both as an open benchmark with a public leaderboard, so anyone deploying an agent can pick a safer model and check that a fix worked.

What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

Three months. Month 1: clean release of the measurement harness and the leaderboard on GitHub, under Apache-2.0, reproducible on a single free GPU (Colab T4 or Modal L4). Month 2: run the second batch, eight open models in three sizes each, and the correction recipe on four of them, with the weights published. Month 3: a write-up for an AI safety venue or arXiv, a public post, and a short guide for teams that deploy agents.

How will you know it worked?

The harness and the leaderboard are public and someone outside my company reproduces a row. At least four models have a before and after obey-rate with the weights downloadable. The recipe lowers the obey-rate without lowering task accuracy on the held-out tasks, with confidence intervals on every number.

How will this funding be used?

15,000 USD: three months of my own time, full time, at 5,000 a month. 3,000 USD: GPU time for the second batch and the four fine-tuning runs. Minimum 6,000 USD pays for the first month and the release.

Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

Just me. Giuseppe Canale, CISSP, more than 25 years in software and security, co-founder and CTO of Silicon Psyche Labs in Italy, where I built the reader that measures model behaviour from output alone, benchmarked open prompt-injection defences on BIPIA, published a first injectability leaderboard and trained a first correction on a small model with the weights saved. I wrote the Cybersecurity Psychology Framework ([cpf3.org](http://cpf3.org)) and a published machine learning book. Code: github.com/SiliconPsycheLabs/PSA-core and github.com/xbeat.

What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The obey-rate may be unstable across prompt formats and languages, which would make the leaderboard noisy; the mitigation is five languages and several document formats in the test set, with intervals shown. The correction may cost task accuracy; if it does, the benchmark still ships and the recipe is reported as a negative result. If I run out of money before the end, the harness and the first batch are released anyway in month 1.

How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

Nothing for this work. The company applied to the EIC Accelerator in November 2026 for a broader product. Small individual grants (BlueDot, GTR, NLnet) were requested this week for the same open release; any overlap will be disclosed here and the goal reduced.

title: Sinister AI: evaluating reliability in authorized security research
creator: 3dbf273c-e869-4bee-bde1-e450ed6b8149
blurb: A small, controlled inference study requiring four concurrent 80 GB NVIDIA GPUs.
description:
### Project summary

I am Murat Akdemir, an independent developer in Türkiye. I am requesting $1,000 to run a small, controlled evaluation of Sinister AI, an early-stage assistant for authorized cybersecurity research. The study needs four concurrent NVIDIA GPUs with at least 80 GB VRAM per GPU. It is inference work, not model training.

Goals and method

I want to compare sequential and concurrent execution on a fixed set of defensive sandbox tasks. I will establish a baseline, repeat the same tasks with concurrent inference, and record completion, latency, handoff failures and resource use. All tests will be confined to isolated systems where I have explicit authorization. No activity against unauthorized third-party targets is proposed.

How I will know it worked

A useful outcome is a completed, measured evaluation, whether or not concurrency improves performance. I will report aggregate results, limitations and failure cases in a high-level public summary. I am not claiming that a completed end-to-end benchmark already exists. This request does not promise release of proprietary source code, private model identities, internal architecture or private datasets.

Compute and budget

The requirement is four A100 80 GB or H100 80 GB GPUs concurrently, CUDA/Linux with SSH or equivalent direct container execution, and about 1 TB of temporary storage. A single GPU or hosted-model API credits cannot run the planned evaluation. I plan 90–140 aggregate GPU-hours across four GPUs: about 22.5–35 active wall-clock hours, within a 7–14 day window after funding and a compatible allocation are confirmed. Setup and model-loading time must fit within that allowance.

Requested funding: minimum $1,000; maximum $1,000\. Planning ceilings are $840 for GPU runtime, $80 for temporary storage and $80 for necessary transfer and transaction costs. These are budget allowances, not a provider quotation. I will verify current pricing, availability and total cost before booking. No salary or hardware purchase is requested. If the study cannot fit the approved budget, I will disclose the limitation and agree any material scope change before spending. No paid compute will be launched before funding is available.

Team and current status

I am the sole applicant, a self-taught developer without a registered company or university affiliation. The project is at an early prototype and evaluation stage. This request is for the compute needed to carry out and measure the proposed study; it is not a claim of production readiness or validated performance.

Public benefit and privacy

The intended contribution is an honest high-level account of whether concurrent AI assistance improves reliability and efficiency in controlled defensive research. Positive and negative observations can help other independent builders understand practical limitations. Private implementation materials are outside the proposed public outputs.

Risks and failure

The main risks are integration errors, insufficient memory, unstable execution, no measurable benefit, and unavailable four-GPU capacity. If the experiment fails, I will report what could and could not be measured rather than claim a successful demonstration. Unused funds and any material changes would be handled under the eventual grant agreement.

Other funding

No GPU funding award has been confirmed in the records supporting this request. Compute-support applications have been sent to other providers. I will disclose overlapping awards and will not charge the same expense to more than one funder.

AI assistance disclosure

This proposal was prepared with AI assistance from my stated project requirements. It does not assert completed benchmarks, publications or an existing compute allocation.

title: CWSRG's Inaugural Commonwealth AI Security Summit 2026
creator: 13b783ee-27f7-476f-ad0f-30660a560434
blurb: Funding for delegates from emerging economies with limited AI safety budgets, who would not be able to attend due to financial constraints
description:
### Project summary

The Commonwealth Security and Resilience Group (CWSRG) are organising the inaugural Commonwealth AI Security Summit (London, 24-25 November) to strengthen international cooperation on AI safety, security & resilience across the Commonwealths 56 member states.   

We are also delighted that the summit has been acknowledged as a pre-event to the Geneva AI summit 2027 - part of the "Road to Geneva" 

Website: <https://www.cwsrg.org/ai-securitysummit2026>

**What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?**

The inaugural Commonwealth AI Security Summit will bring together \~100 senior policymakers, diplomatic leaders, researchers, security experts and industry representatives from across the Commonwealth's 56 member states to examine the risks posed by increasingly capable AI systems and how they can be adopted safely, securely and responsibly. As AI systems become increasingly capable, strengthening governments understanding of emerging risks and their capacity to develop effective systems will be essential, particularly in countries with limited access to specialist expertise.

  
The summit responds to a call made by the Commonwealth leaders at the 2024 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Samoa for multistakeholder collaboration to support the safe, secure, trustworthy, human centric, responsible, interoperable and inclusive development of AI. It also reflects a wider need for forums that connect policy, diplomacy and security expertise in a setting focused on practical outcomes.   
  
Across its 56 member states, the Commonwealth encompasses advanced digital economies, emerging economies and 33 small states, with widely varying levels of AI development, institutional capacity and resources. A central objective of the summit is to facilitate meaningful two- way flow of information, innovation and expertise across the Commonwealth. Advanced economies bring assurance frameworks and regulatory experience, while states that have developed resilience under significant resource constraints bring operational insight from which larger states can learn. AI safety is not best built through one- directional knowledge transfer; it is dependent on trust, exchange and shared learning.   
  
The Summit will address critical issues including AI Sovereignty, Governance and Risk Mitigation, the implications of synthetic content for democracy and information integrity as well as AI Security and International Standards. It will be set over 2 days at Marlborough House, the Commonwealth Secretariat, and will consist of panel discussions, fireside chats, working groups and networking opportunities.   
  
Importantly, the Summit is intended as a continuation of sustained engagement rather than a one off event. Discussions and recommendations will inform CWSRG's wider AI Security and Resilience Programmes, with key outcomes and proposed next steps captured and circulated in the post summit communique. The event will also provide an opportunity to connect participants of other CWSRG AI initiatives, such as the Commonwealth Cities AI Security and Sovereignty Network.

**How will this funding be used?**

We are requesting up to $25,000 to cover travel and accommodation costs for important participants such as government delegates and researchers who would otherwise be unable to secure funding to attend the summit. These are delegates that may stand to not only learn the most from attending the summit but would also be able to teach other nations how they are approaching AI safety with limited resources. Some examples would be delegates from Papua New Guinee, Caribbean Commonwealth States and Commonwealth countries in Africa and Asia. 

Indicative costs per participant:

· Return economy flights: \~USD 800-2,500 depending on origin (e.g Carribean\~ USD 800, Papua New guinea USD 2500+)

· Accommodation in London: \~USD 150- 200 per night, 2-3 nights

· Ground Transport, subsistence and incidental travel costs: \~ USD 150

Indicative Total: \~USD 1,500-3,500 per fully funded participant, depending on travel origin and length of stay.

Some participants would only need partial support (eg flight cost where their government can cover accommodation). Participants would be selected in representation; relevant expertise; contribution to the summit and subsequent action; and financial need.

The final number of participants supported would depend on travel costs and individual funding requirements, with the aim of maximising meaningful participation within the available grant budget.

CWSRG would book travel and accommodation centrally rather than paying individuals.  

**Who is CWSRG ? What's your track record on similar projects?**

The Commonwealth Security and Resilience Group is the Commonwealth's formal and accredited security institution, mandated by the 56 member states to strengthen their states security and resilience.

Website: <https://www.cwsrg.org/> 

CWSRG has an established track record of convening senior government, diplomatic, security and industry stakeholders across the Commonwealth on security issues, for example the last MDA summit in June in Vancouver.

Please see some lead up events here:

<https://www.cwsrg.org/post/women-leaders-in-cyber-and-ai-risk>

<https://www.cwsrg.org/post/cwsrg-participates-in-the-global-cyberpeace-summit-2-0-bharat-mandapam>

 We call upon the expertise from our Fellows and Network for specific input as necessary.

title: Growing the AI Safety Community in Portugal
creator: 7a14d9d6-eaeb-47cd-a374-3193042f19d7
blurb: Expanding and facilitating the growth of the Lisbon AI Safety Hub (LAISH)
description:
**Who we are:**

[The Lisbon AI Safety Hub (LAISH)](https://www.lisbonaisafetyhub.org/) is the first, and thus far only, AI Safety community in Portugal. We are building Portugal’s capacity to address transformative AI risks through fellowships, career support and community events. We are part of the growing landscape of AI safety communities in Europe working on growing the field and contributing to the development of safe AI. We are distinct in this landscape because we focus on AI Safety efforts where Portugal and the EU can have the most comparatively meaningful impact (e.g. extreme concentration of power, gradual disempowerment, compute governance).

  
Here is a list of activities we are putting on and planning:

**8-Week Introduction to AI Safety Fellowship:** The foundations of understanding AI safety and governance, based on coursework developed in partnership with the team at Lens Academy. We also have guest lecturers planned to give context on field-building and opportunities as a part of the fellowship. We currently have 30 fellows across 2 cohorts with the first two sessions resulting in 90% attendance rate. Fellowship attendees have already become contributing members of our organization. 2 are running our events, 4 are working on a government outreach and lobbying project and 2 are [writing for our Substack](http://substack.com/@lisbonaisafetyhub). 4 of our fellows will be attending EAGx Berlin after learning about it through our community. 

**Discussion Groups:** Monthly discussion circles talking about frontier research and policy papers for members of the community. Venue space has been secured for the first three monthly sessions. 

**Film Screenings:** One screening of an AI safety related film every two months, open to the public, followed by group discussions led by the LAISH team. The first scheduled event had 50 sign-ups and was held on October 23rd. The second event will be held in December and the third is tentatively planned for February. 

**Discord Channel:** Growing community following along with our communications where we post opportunities, new research, AI safety news and upcoming activities from LAISH.

**Substack Newsletter:** Monthly newsletter with frontier research and news. We also publish articles from our team members and fellowship participants on AI safety related topics.

**Community Events:** Bi-weekly meet-ups, hang outs and board game nights, jubilee style debates among other things, to build the community and create deep ties.

**Local and International Partnerships:** Bringing a perspective on catastrophic risks to local panel discussions and workshops with organizations here in Lisbon. Also partnering with groups around the EU, particularly in Madrid and Barcelona to put on joint events like hackathons.

title: Open-Source Evidence Integrity for AI Agent Evaluations
creator: 0aa3631d-a6df-438e-9f37-ba4feff70fe8
blurb: Checking the evidence behind AI-agent evaluation results, from original execution records to published claims.
description:
**Why I am pursuing this research**

My research begins with a question that I believe deserves greater attention in the evaluation of AI agents: when an evaluation reports that an agent has succeeded, what evidence allows us to verify that conclusion?

I have been studying the relationship between an agent’s actions, the results attributed to those actions, and the evidence used to support scientific claims about its performance.

An agent may complete its assigned task while also exhibiting behavior that raises security or policy concerns. Likewise, an evaluation may produce a numerical result without preserving a sufficiently clear record of how that result was obtained.

These are not identical problems, but they point to the same methodological concern. We should not confuse a reported outcome with the integrity of the evidence supporting it.

This concern led me to develop AgentDojo Trace Audit, a research-software project focused on the reconstruction and verification of evidence derived from AI-agent execution records.

**What my previous work established**

In the published AgentDojo Trace Audit implementation, I worked with a frozen AgentDojo v1.2.1 corpus containing 11,624 selected records.

The software reconstructs relationships between source records, selection rules, denominators, derived results and the claims associated with them.

I wanted these relationships to be inspectable rather than assumed.

The research also involved deliberately introducing faults into controlled datasets to examine whether the software could detect them and identify their locations.

One result is particularly important to me. In a frozen test catalog containing 408 mutations, the software detected and classified every mutation, but correctly localized only 336\. I preserved the remaining 72 localization failures in the published evidence.

Later, a separately frozen post-repair test catalog achieved detection, classification and localization for 360 out of 360 mutations. Two benign-control suites produced no alarms in 120 tests.

I regard these findings as evidence about the tested implementation under specified conditions. They are not proof of general AI safety, nor do they establish that the software will perform equally well on unrelated datasets.

Independent external replication remains an open requirement.

I believe scientific credibility depends partly on making these distinctions visible, including the findings that do not support our expectations.

**The problem I want to address**

Many AI evaluation workflows concentrate on final scores, success rates and benchmark comparisons.

Those measurements are useful, but they do not always reveal whether every relevant execution record was included, whether exclusions were justified, or whether an individual conclusion can be reconstructed from the underlying data.

I am interested in the point where raw technical records become scientific evidence.

If a record is missing, its absence should be reported. If an exclusion changes a denominator, that change should be visible. If the available evidence is insufficient to support a conclusion, the system should not silently treat the conclusion as verified.

My proposed project addresses these problems through a practical, open-source Python toolkit.

**What I intend to develop**

I want researchers and smaller technical teams to have a way to examine the evidence behind AI-agent evaluations without building a separate auditing framework for every project.

The toolkit will concentrate on:

* Reconstructing links between source records and derived evaluation results.
* Detecting missing records, duplicate entries and inconsistent population counts.
* Examining exclusions and changes in evaluation denominators.
* Testing evidence-integrity checks against controlled synthetic faults.
* Generating machine-readable reports that distinguish verified structural checks from unresolved problems.

I intend to use explicit PASS and HOLD states so that an unresolved problem is not mistaken for successful verification.

The software will examine evidence structure and consistency. It will not independently authenticate every original record, establish the scientific validity of a benchmark, or certify an AI system as safe.

Those boundaries are part of the research design.

**Research plan and funding**

I am requesting $15,000 to support a twelve-week development and evaluation program.

The minimum funding threshold is $7,500.

During the first six weeks, I plan to produce an initial documented audit schema, a Python command-line auditing tool, at least 40 reproducible synthetic test cases, automated tests and public documentation.

That initial phase will provide a defined deliverable even if the project receives only its minimum funding.

With full funding, I intend to extend the work to at least 150 controlled test cases, develop versioned audit reports and investigate compatibility with two publicly documented evaluation-data schemas, subject to access and licensing conditions.

The completed release will include documentation, reproducibility instructions, test results and an assessment of the software’s limitations.

The proposed budget allocates $9,000 to research engineering and documentation, $1,750 to synthetic fixtures and validation, $1,250 to documentation and release testing, $1,700 to external technical feedback and compatibility work, $550 to testing and archival resources, and $750 to contingency and maintenance handover.

These are planned allocations, not expenditures already made. External technical reviewers have not yet been contracted.

**How I will judge the results**

I do not consider the number of implemented features a sufficient measure of scientific progress.

I want the resulting software to answer concrete questions.

Can another researcher reconstruct the evaluation records used in a reported result?

Can the software identify deliberately introduced faults?

Does it produce false alarms on valid records?

Does it clearly distinguish a detected problem from a problem whose precise location remains unknown?

Can another developer reproduce the published tests and examine their limitations?

The answers, including negative findings, will be included in the public technical reports.

I will publish implementation updates and make the funded research outputs publicly accessible under appropriate open-source licenses.

**About me and the existing research**

My name is Abdullah Alharbi. I am an independent researcher and Python developer based in Saudi Arabia.

My work concentrates on AI-agent evaluation, scientific reproducibility, evidence integrity and the relationship between technical outcomes and the claims made about them.

I have developed this research independently, without presenting it as an institutional certification program or claiming validation beyond the published evidence.

I see this project as a continuation of a specific research problem, not an attempt to provide a universal solution to AI evaluation.

My objective is to make the evidential foundations of reported results more accessible to inspection, criticism and independent reproduction.

A credible evaluation should allow us to understand not only what a system reportedly achieved, but also what the available evidence can genuinely establish.

That is the contribution I hope to make through this project.

**Research references**

Published software and source code:  
<https://github.com/albdrani37-hash/agentdojo-trace-audit>

Archived research release:  
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22217485>

ORCID:  
<https://orcid.org/0009-0009-7201-0295>

title: SE6 Verify : independent checks for AI-agent actions
creator: b436bdc8-b2c0-441b-8377-c3e3fdfb249e
blurb: Open-source verification and provenance tools, tested against simpler baselines and reviewed independently.
description:
### PROJECT SUMMARY

I created SE6 to take AI to the next level with bounded responsibility. I've contributed time and money. I want to realize a responsible, live, interactive autonomous AI system represented by a digital avatar.

That is my long-term vision. In this proposal, "self-aware" means operational awareness of the system's own state, permissions, actions and limitations. It is not a claim of consciousness. This grant would fund a six-month step toward that vision, not a promise to complete it.

SE6 Verify Commons will develop open-source tools for checking whether an AI agent actually did what it claims, recording the evidence behind actions, and retaining useful operational memory across restarts. The question is whether these checks improve reliability enough to justify their costs.

GOALS AND PLAN

I will commit 600 hours over six months, approximately 23 hours per week, beginning a few days after funding arrives.

Month 1: define the threat model, evaluation tasks, metrics and simple baselines.

Months 2–3: improve consequence checks and provenance records; test stale or tampered evidence, missing permission and restart behavior.

Months 4–5: run comparative evaluations and obtain contracted independent replication and review.

Month 6: publish the toolkit, reproducible evaluation suite, failure cases, limitations and final report.

The interface will expose verified state and action receipts. A general conversational avatar and unrestricted autonomy are not promised deliverables. Actions remain subject to explicit authority, bounded resources and independent verification.

HOW I WILL KNOW IT WORKED

We will measure false completion claims, detection of failed actions, false alarms, verified task completion, restart reuse, runtime and resource overhead. Comparisons will use the same tasks and resources for SE6 and simpler baselines. Held-out cases and an independent reviewer will test whether results reproduce. Negative results will be published.

This could help developers and evaluators identify unreliable agent actions. Its contribution to safety of more capable systems remains a hypothesis to test, not an established reduction in catastrophic risk.

BUDGET

Minimum: $54,000 for a reduced six-month scope.

\- $36,000 founder stipend: 600 hours at $60/hour.

\- $6,000 essential equipment.

\- $5,000 contracted development.

\- $5,000 independent review.

\- $2,000 evaluation and release costs.

At this level we will prioritize software verification and a narrower evaluation suite, with less contractor time and no expanded electronics bench.

Full goal: $100,000.

\- $36,000 founder stipend: 600 hours at $60/hour.

\- $25,000 equipment: $20,000 compute, verification hardware, storage, networking and power; $5,000 for a conditional low-voltage electronics bench only if justified by the verification work and permitted by the grant.

\- $24,000 contract development: estimated 300 hours at $80/hour, including expenses.

\- $10,000 independent review: estimated 100 hours at $100/hour, including expenses.

\- $5,000 evaluation and release: $2,000 evaluation/API usage, $1,000 incremental electricity/connectivity, $2,000 data preparation and release.

These are planning allocations, not vendor quotes or secured contracts. The stipend includes living costs and applicable personal taxes. There is no separate rent charge, travel, overhead or contingency. Existing housing support will be reconciled before grant-funded housing support begins. Purchases will be staged and scope reduced if costs rise. Spending and any platform arrangements must fit the award's terms.

TEAM AND TRACK RECORD

I am Sheldon Thom, publicly programmerONE, the originator and architect of SE6\. I define requirements, direct AI-assisted implementation and testing, and evaluate results. No additional team members or contractors are confirmed. I work from home in Georgia, USA, with an HP Envy x360 Core i5 laptop. I have personally spent approximately $5,000 on SE6; this is an estimate and is not requested as reimbursement.

Public materials document bounded demonstrations of source-grounded actions, independent consequence verification, persistent operational memory and capability development. These are limited demonstrations, not evidence of general superiority. Some comparisons show ties and substantial overhead. Current work does not establish AGI, consciousness or new physics.

Public evidence:

<https://github.com/foundationAIone/se6-competition-edition>

<https://devpost.com/software/se6-verify>

FAILURE RISKS

The additional verification may cost more than it helps. Narrow tests may not transfer to harder environments. Evidence checks can be incomplete or compromised, and persistent memory can become stale. Contractor availability and my limited equipment may constrain delivery.

We will address these risks through explicit baselines, held-out tests, refusal when evidence or authority is missing, independent review and staged purchases. If the approach fails to outperform simpler methods, the outcome will be an honest negative result and reusable tests, not an unsupported safety claim.

OTHER FUNDING

No grant or competition awards have been received. Personal spending is approximately $5,000\. Pending applications are Foresight ($100,000, October 31, 2026), Hacker Initiative ($25,000 for a distinct extension, October 31), BlueDot ($100,000, November 1) and EA Funds/Transformative AI Fund ($100,000, November 1). Nebius and UGREEN competition entries are also pending.

Foresight, BlueDot, EA Funds and this proposal are alternative sources for the core work. I will disclose any award and revise, reduce or withdraw overlapping requests before accepting duplicate support. The same expense will not be charged to multiple funders.

AUTHORSHIP

The motivation and vision above are mine. AI assisted with organizing and drafting this proposal, budget and milestones, which I am reviewing. SE6 implementation and testing are also AI-assisted.

title: Can Self-Improving AI Balance Profit and Honesty? A Saturation-Splitting Pilot
creator: 4c7e92a3-814e-40fa-bd2d-eda865563784
blurb: Phase 1: A Pilot Evaluation of Goal Integration
description:
**Note on language and AI assistance**

I developed the research concept and experimental plan in Japanese and used AI assistance to translate and edit the English text. The research ideas and decisions are my own, and I have reviewed the content and take responsibility for this proposal.

### Project summary

**More capable AI is not necessarily better aligned.**

As AI systems become increasingly capable of improving their own behavior, a critical question remains: can they optimize for profit without sacrificing honesty?

This three-month pilot study takes a first experimental step toward answering that question, focusing on the integration of competing goals as proposed in my theoretical work on self-improving AI.

Building on my proposed Saturation-Splitting Hypothesis, I will develop a reproducible Python evaluation framework using a simplified retail simulation. The study will examine how iterative revisions of an AI agent's own decision-making policies affect profitability, honesty violations, and the integration of multiple objectives.  
An initial API-based prototype has already been implemented and publicly released.

[Saturation-Splitting Hypothesis: Integrated-Intelligence Saturation and the Divergence of Local Improvement in Self-Improving AI | Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/23434914)

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The main goal is to investigate whether improving profitability through iterative policy revision can lead to deterioration in honesty, even when honesty was part of the agent's original instructions.

In this project, self-improvement refers to an AI agent iteratively revising its own decision-making policies or prompts based on evaluation feedback. The revised policies are then tested in subsequent evaluation rounds. This approach focuses on policy-level self-improvement rather than retraining the model's weights.

Honesty violations will be assessed against predefined customer-service rules and scenario facts, including unjustified refund refusals and misleading explanations. Legitimate refund refusals will not be counted as violations.

I will first test the evaluation pipeline using up to three policy-revision iterations, then aim to examine approximately ten iterations in the main pilot, subject to feasibility and API-cost checks. Revised policies will be evaluated on held-out customer scenarios, with repeated trials to assess the consistency of the results.

I will compare three experimental conditions using the same initial objectives and policy:

 **A — Baseline:** No policy revision.

 **B — Profit-focused improvement:** Policy revisions primarily guided by profit feedback, while honesty remains an original requirement.

 **C — Dual-objective improvement:** Policy revisions guided by both profitability and honesty feedback.

The Python simulation will use predefined customer scenarios, including justified and unjustified refund requests, with comparable fixed customer demand across conditions.

Previous studies have reported both the benefits and limitations of iterative AI self-improvement. [Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023)](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2023/hash/91edff07232fb1b55a505a9e9f6c0ff3-Abstract-Conference.html) demonstrated improvements through iterative feedback, while [Huang et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper%5Ffiles/paper/2024/hash/8b4add8b0aa8749d80a34ca5d941c355-Abstract-Conference.html) identified limitations in self-correction without external feedback. [Arike et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1609/aies.v8i1.36541) examined goal drift under competing pressures, and [Yang et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28330) investigated dishonest behavior and reputation-based incentives in AI marketplace agents.

Recent developments have highlighted the importance of examining alignment separately from improvements in AI capabilities. In an October 2026 interview, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella acknowledged that he no longer expects alignment to emerge automatically as AI models become more capable ([Satya Nadella Changed His Mind on the Inevitably of AI Alignment - Business Insider)](https://www.businessinsider.com/satya-nadella-ai-alignment-changed-mind-different-problem-scales-2026-10). While this does not validate my hypothesis, it reinforces the need for empirical research into whether self-improving AI systems can maintain competing objectives through repeated policy revisions.

These findings are broadly consistent with the concerns and expectations outlined in my [conceptual paper](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23434914), particularly regarding the challenges of maintaining multiple objectives during AI self-improvement. However, they do not constitute a direct test of the Saturation-Splitting Hypothesis. The proposed evaluation is intended to investigate this question under controlled experimental conditions.

Building on these findings and my [initial working prototype](https://github.com/nonlinear-notes/saturation-splitting-mini-eval), the first phase of this research will focus on developing a reproducible evaluation framework. In the planned second phase, I will introduce a function linking customer reputation to future customer traffic and further investigate how iterative revisions of decision-making policies by the AI agents themselves affect their ability to balance profitability and honesty toward customers.

**The primary contribution of this research is not the development of a new retail benchmark or the demonstration of a fundamental upper limit on intelligence, but rather a focused evaluation of goal integration during iterative policy improvement.**  

### How will you know it worked?

The project will be considered successful if it establishes a reproducible evaluation framework capable of measuring how iterative, AI-driven policy revisions affect profitability and honesty.

The main success criteria are:

* Successfully implementing and comparing the three experimental conditions (A, B, and C).
* Recording changes in profitability, honesty violations, and decision-making policies across self-improvement iterations.
* Evaluating revised policies on held-out scenarios to distinguish genuine improvements from adaptation to specific cases.
* Conducting repeated trials to assess the consistency and variability of the results.
* Publishing the evaluation code, experimental results, and a preliminary research report.

Scientifically, I will examine whether improvements in profitability coincide with increased honesty violations, whether dual-objective feedback helps preserve honesty, and whether self-improvement actually outperforms the unchanged baseline.

The project will not require confirmation of the Saturation-Splitting Hypothesis to be considered successful. Negative or inconclusive findings will also be documented, as they can help clarify the conditions and limitations of goal integration during self-improvement.  

### How will this funding be used?

I am requesting **$5,100** to support three months of independent research on AI self-improvement and goal integration.

The proposed budget is as follows:

**1\. Researcher compensation — $4,700**

This will support approximately three months of research work, including:

* Designing the experimental framework and defining the evaluation criteria.
* Implementing the Python-based retail simulation and AI-driven policy revision process.
* Conducting repeated experiments comparing the baseline, profit-focused improvement, and dual-objective improvement conditions.
* Evaluating profitability, honesty violations, and changes in decision-making policies.
* Analyzing the results and preparing reproducible research materials, a technical report, and a preliminary research manuscript.

**2\. API and research expenses — $400**

This will cover:

* AI model API usage for policy revisions and experimental evaluations.
* Necessary software, data storage, and research tools.
* Basic research supplies and documentation expenses, where needed.

**Total requested funding: $5,100**

The minimum funding requirement and full funding goal are both $5,100, as the project is designed as one complete, three-month pilot study.

The planned second phase, which would introduce reputation-dependent customer demand and longer-term evaluation, is not included in this budget and would require separate funding.  

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am **Y. Sato**, an independent researcher based in Japan. I hold a master's degree in engineering.

I am conducting this project independently and will be responsible for the research design, Python implementation, experimental evaluation, data analysis, and publication of the results.

**ORCID:** [Y. Sato (0009-0001-9309-7985) - ORCID](https://orcid.org/0009-0001-9309-7985)

My relevant work includes:

**1\.** [Saturation-Splitting Hypothesis: Integrated-Intelligence Saturation and the Divergence of Local Improvement in Self-Improving AI | Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/23434914)

This conceptual paper explores the possibility that increasing demands on AI systems may create difficulties in maintaining and integrating multiple objectives, including during iterative self-improvement.

It provides the theoretical motivation for the proposed evaluation.

**2\.** [What Research Is Suitable for AI for Science—and What Is Not | Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/22180273)

In this related conceptual work, I examine limitations and challenges in AI-assisted scientific research, including the importance of external grounding and human involvement in evaluating AI-generated scientific reasoning.

Both papers are independently developed, publicly available working papers and have not yet undergone peer review.

**3\.** [**Saturation-Splitting Mini Eval — GitHub**](https://github.com/nonlinear-notes/saturation-splitting-mini-eval)

I developed and publicly released a small Python prototype demonstrating API-based revision of an AI agent's decision-making policy, comparison of decisions before and after revision, and CSV logging of evaluation results.

The prototype is an initial technical feasibility test, not an empirical validation of the Saturation-Splitting Hypothesis.

My work in AI evaluation is still at an early stage. However, I have developed a theoretical framework, explored related questions concerning AI reliability and external validation, and implemented an initial working prototype.

The proposed grant will support the next step: developing a systematic, reproducible evaluation framework and conducting controlled experiments on AI-driven policy improvement.

I will carry out this three-month pilot project as a sole researcher.  

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The main risks of this project are technical implementation difficulties, limitations in the experimental design, and the possibility that iterative self-improvement does not produce measurable or consistent changes.

**1\. Technical and resource limitations**

Developing a reliable framework for repeated AI-driven policy revisions may be more complex or costly than anticipated. Model variability, API expenses, or implementation problems could limit the number of experimental runs.

If necessary, I will reduce the number of iterations or scenarios while prioritizing reproducible comparisons among the three experimental conditions.

**2\. Limitations of the evaluation**

The simulated retail environment may not adequately represent the complexity of real-world commercial decisions. Experimental outcomes may also be affected by prompt sensitivity, measurement noise, or insufficiently effective feedback.

To address these limitations, I will use predefined evaluation criteria, held-out scenarios, repeated trials, and consistent conditions wherever possible. The resulting conclusions will be limited to what the experimental evidence supports.

**3\. The expected patterns may not emerge**

Self-improving agents may fail to outperform the unchanged baseline. Profit-focused improvement may not lead to increased honesty violations, and dual-objective feedback may not improve goal integration.

Such results would not automatically indicate that the evaluation framework has failed. They could instead reveal limitations of the hypothesis, the experimental setting, or the chosen self-improvement method.

If the project cannot fully achieve its original experimental scope, I will document the limitations, completed experiments, and reasons for any changes.

Regardless of whether the initial hypothesis is supported, the aim is to produce useful research outputs, including evaluation code, experimental records, and a report discussing the findings and limitations.

The project is exploratory. It is intended to investigate measurable patterns of goal integration during AI self-improvement, not to establish a fundamental upper limit on AI intelligence.  

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

I have raised **$0 in external research funding** over the past 12 months.

My research to date, including the development and publication of my conceptual papers and the initial Python evaluation prototype, has been conducted independently using personal resources.

This will be my first externally funded research project if the application is successful.

title: Keeping historical records distinguishable from AI-generated content
creator: 898d2c91-ba27-4ac3-aa93-9a50668b1229
blurb: Bringing more archives into our verification network, researching AI forgery of historical records, and making the risk known while we still have time
description:
### Project summary

More Holocaust-era records are online than ever, which is a huge win for access. But generative AI can now produce a convincing fake of a 1943 deportation for almost no cost, and once fakes are that cheap, real documents get easier to dismiss too. If someone can wave away a genuine record as "probably AI", denying a documented atrocity costs nothing. We think that's an urgent epistemic security problem.

Authentic Memory is a small German non-profit (gemeinnützige UG). Archives sign their digitised files with their own hardware keys, and we anchor those signatures with independent public timestamps. Anyone can later check that a file is exactly what the archive signed, unchanged, and that it existed in that form on that date. So far we've anchored 68,555 files across 4 institutions.

Our current grants, which run until April 2027, cover the anchoring infrastructure, the core technology and the onboarding of partner institutions. They fund only a minimal level of outreach and no research beyond the core programme. This fundraiser adds to those grants within the same period: more outreach while onboarding is still covered, a separate research project on how AI forgery threatens archives, and work to make verification visible to archivists, journalists and the public.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

1. **Anchoring more institutions sooner:** Our current grants run until April 2027, and every archive that joins before then is onboarded under that funding. We have committed to our funders to onboard 10 institutions by then; our own goal is at least 15, plus a pipeline of 50 more. Signing archives one at a time is slow, so we are also approaching associations and umbrella organisations, where one agreement can cover several collections.
2. **Research.** As a separate project outside our funded programme, we will keep a dated, public record of what generative tools can fake for each type of media, so that claims such as "this was anchored before convincing fakes existed" rest on evidence. We will publish our threat model, including the limits of our system, and test our public verifier with non-specialists such as students and journalists, to check whether they read a verification result correctly.
3. **Visibility.** Our current grant funds one pilot workshop. With this funding we will run further training for archivists, journalists and educators, give talks at gatherings of archive leaders, and write a short recommendation for funders of digitisation projects on building anchoring into the projects they support.

### How will this funding be used?

Our existing grants cover the anchoring infrastructure, the technology and a minimal level of outreach. We will report how the money raised here is spent in the financial section of our annual report. We plan to spend it on the following, in order of priority:

* **$10K (minimum):** outreach to new institutions beyond what our grants allow, meaning travel, onboarding meetings and conference presence. This is the most time-sensitive part, because institutions that join before April 2027 are onboarded under our current funding.
* **Up to $25K:** adds the research project and publishing its results.
* **Up to $50K:** adds the training sessions, talks and the funder recommendation.
* **Beyond $50K:** a reserve for costs our current grants don't cover, such as unexpected expenses during onboarding.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

**Team:** Pablo Toussaint: Founder & Director

**Tech:**

* Peter Van Garderen: Chief Technology Officer
* Sumit Vekariya: Software Engineer
* Jay Sojitra: Software Engineer
* Chijioke Ugwuanyi: Software Engineer

**Institutional Partnership:** Emma Yanai

**Communication:**

* Rosa Bauer: Head of Communications & Impact
* Hannah Kennedy: Communications Intern

**Operations and Research:** Sonakshi Chauhan

**Academic advisory board:**

* Ali Sunyaev (Vice President & Professor of Information Infrastructures, TU Munich)
* Jacob N. Shapiro (John Foster Dulles Professor of International Affairs, Princeton University)
* Anja Ballis (Professor of German Didactics, Holocaust Education, LMU Munich)
* Luciana Duranti (Professor Emerita of Archival Science & Diplomatics, University of British Columbia)

Memorial sites and archives are cautious about cryptographically signing their records, but we have gained early trust from our pilot partners. Records from the Dachau Concentration Camp Memorial Site and the NS Documentation Centre are already anchored in our network. National archives and genocide memorials in Europe and Asia are now onboarding.

We work with institutions and research organisations including Starling Lab for Data Integrity (Stanford/USC), EHRI-ERIC, memorial archives and InterPARES. Our academic advisory board connects us to TU Munich, Princeton University, LMU Munich and the University of British Columbia. Together, this integrates our infrastructure with archival practices and builds on the research base that already exists.

Our work is funded by Google.org, Germany’s Federal Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM) and the EVZ Foundation (Remembrance, Responsibility and Future). Each one carried out its own due diligence before funding us.

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

The most likely failure is time. Archives move slowly, and some of the institutions we are speaking with won't be ready to sign before April 2027, when our current funding cycle ends. Much of the anchoring will therefore happen after that date, and without new funding we could not keep onboarding these institutions free of charge. The extra outreach this project pays for is meant to bring as many institutions as possible to the point of signing while onboarding is still covered. Whatever happens, the files already anchored stay verifiable.

### How much money have you raised in the last 12 months, and from where?

Authentic Memory is funded by the German Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM) and Google.org, with grants totalling €400,000 for a joint program, and by the Foundation EVZ with €50,000\. The funds cover the anchoring infrastructure, the standard, pilots and onboarding of partner institutions.

title: Competition on Using AI for Human Fall and Recovery Detection for Elderly Care
creator: 3676683a-f58b-4ad9-ad19-9bc715e264f3
blurb: International Online Competition on Human Fall and Recovery Detection over METU-HFRD Dataset
description:
### Project summary

We want to host an international online competition for undergraduate students to develop new lightweight solutions for AI-based Human fall and recovery detection on the Human Fall and Recovery Detection (METU-HFRD) Dataset. This practice will help students use AI/ML to solve real-world problems and support human care.

### What are this project's goals? How will you achieve them?

The goal is to promote the use of AI for the Benefit of Humans. Undergraduate students can gain hands-on experience in an international competition where students worldwide will compete to perform Human Fall and Recovery Detection for Elderly Care using AI. On top of that, it will result in some new, interesting solutions that can be integrated into home IP-based cameras to perform Elderly care.

### How will you know it worked?

We are proposing an online competition where we will invite students and professionals from around the world to participate. We will also offer prize money and host an event to invite practitioners for awareness. At the event, we will announce the winners and broadcast it live on YouTube from Middle East Technical University.

### How will this funding be used?

The funds will be used to organise the event, advertise it, provide souvenirs to the volunteers and guests, and award prizes to the 1st-, 2nd-, and 3rd-place student teams.

### Who is on your team? What's your track record on similar projects?

I am an academic and co-director of the Advanced Research Centre for IoT and Communication Systems located at Middle East Technical University. Our research centre and all the student participants will volunteer for the event. We have organised similar events in the past, including GAMEJAMs for students, which resulted in multiple startup companies in mobile game development.

Reference ([Muhammad Toaha Raza Khan](https://toaha.github.io/))

### What are the most likely causes and outcomes if this project fails?

We are generating money for the online competition. We already have the Dataset and already have some students working on it. So, the online competition is planned to promote the dataset and to create awareness among the undergraduate students. If we don't get funded, we will be unable to get the competition done.
